purpose: The Australian Government provides funding to eligible higher education providers through the RTP to support their training of domestic and overseas students undertaking research doctorate and research masters degrees (collectively higher degrees by research, HDRs).

Published objectives of the RTP: provide flexible funding to support training domestic students and overseas students undertaking HDRs at Australian higher education providers; deliver graduates with the skills required to build careers in academia and other sectors of the labour market; support collaboration between higher education providers and industry and other research end-users.

The RTP is a research block grant program: Australian Government funding is provided through annual block grants to eligible Australian higher education providers in accordance with section 46-20 of the Higher Education Support Act 2003 and the Higher Education Support (Commonwealth Scholarships) Guidelines 2025. 2026 RTP grant amounts allocated to eligible providers are based on a formula reflecting each provider's relative performance in attracting research income and supporting students to complete HDRs.
study_type: Accredited research doctorate (PhD) - higher degree by research
Accredited research masters degree - higher degree by research
At least two-thirds of the student's time must be spent on research at the eligible Australian university
Full-time or part-time student load (the Guidelines do not restrict part-time students, but providers may award to part-time students only in specific circumstances)

RTP industry internship pathway: an eligible industry internship of at least 3 months and 60 full-time equivalent days of engagement, agreed in writing between the student, the provider and the research end-user, attracts an additional weighting of 2.0 in the provider's funding allocation
official.degree_award: Full research degree (research doctorate or research masters) at an eligible Australian university. Coursework degrees such as a bachelor or masters coursework degree do not qualify as an HDR and are excluded from RTP eligibility.
official.deadline_central_display: No Commonwealth deadline exists. Published wording: 'Universities are responsible for the application, selection and offer processes and deadlines for RTP scholarships.' and 'If you are a prospective higher degree by research (HDR) student interested in applying for an RTP scholarship, you will need to contact your chosen eligible higher education provider (HEP) directly. RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education.'
official.deadline_institutional: Set by each eligible Australian university and published in its RTP scholarship policy, which students are directed to view on the university's webpage. No Commonwealth or provider-wide date is published.
official.travel_coverage: Not published as a travel or airfare component. The published allowances assist with 'the ancillary costs of a HDR', with examples given as relocation costs to undertake a HDR, HDR thesis printing and academic publication costs, and Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) costs for international students and their dependents. No airfare or travel budget figure is published.
official.tuition_rule: Fees offset. Published: 'Fees offset - this requires a university to fully offset the higher degree by research (HDR) tuition fees applicable for a student.' The university, not the Commonwealth directly, determines the amount required to remove the student's liability for tuition fees, so the value of an RTP fees offset varies between universities and potentially between research areas. A provider must inform students of the estimated value of each type of RTP support awarded in the RTP offer letter.
official.tax_status: Published: 'Full-time RTP stipends are considered tax exempt, provided they meet the additional criteria outlined by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Part-time RTP stipends are taxable.' Students are referred to the ATO's scholarship payments webpage for further information.
covered_expenses: Fees offset - full offset of the higher degree by research tuition fees applicable for the student
Stipend to assist students with their living costs while undertaking a HDR
Allowances to assist with the ancillary costs of a HDR
Relocation costs to undertake a HDR (published as an example of an allowance)
HDR thesis printing and academic publication costs (published as examples of allowances)
Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) costs for international students and their dependents (published as an example of an allowance)
not_covered_or_excluded: Bachelor degrees and masters coursework degrees - coursework degrees do not qualify as a HDR and are excluded from RTP eligibility
HDRs undertaken at an overseas university - eligibility requires enrolment at an eligible Australian university
RTP fees offset for a student already receiving an equivalent Australian Government award or scholarship designed to offset HDR fees

For a fees-offset recipient, an RTP fees offset where the student is in receipt of another Commonwealth award or scholarship for the purpose of paying HDR tuition fees (subsection 17(2) applies to domestic students)
Any support beyond the maximum period of support - eligible universities cannot provide extensions beyond the stated maxima

No published list of excluded purchases applies to the stipend itself; use of funds is not restricted in the published Guidelines, but providers set their own policy and any paid-employment restrictions
general_eligibility: Be a domestic or international student enrolled in an accredited research doctorate or research masters degree (an HDR) at an eligible Australian university.
Spend at least two-thirds of your time on research at the eligible Australian university.
For an RTP fees offset specifically, not be receiving an equivalent award or scholarship from the Australian Government that is designed to offset HDR fees.

Meet the eligibility criteria specified in the Higher Education Support (Commonwealth Scholarships) Guidelines 2025 (which replaced the Commonwealth Scholarships Guidelines (Research) 2017 on 3 December 2025).

International students are eligible, but the university in administering RTP scholarships may only spend up to 10% of its RTP funding per grant year on providing scholarships to international students.
Applications may be made to more than one university, or more than once at the same university.
ineligibility_conditions: Enrolling in a bachelor or masters coursework degree - coursework degrees do not qualify as a HDR
Undertaking the HDR at an overseas university rather than an eligible Australian university
Receiving an equivalent Australian Government award or scholarship designed to offset HDR fees, which bars an RTP fees offset
For domestic students in receipt of another Commonwealth award or scholarship for the purpose of paying HDR tuition fees, which bars an RTP fees offset under subsection 17(2)
Not enrolled at an eligible Australian higher education provider
Failing the provider's own additional selection criteria (the Guidelines do not bar a student the provider's criteria bar)

masters: Research masters degrees only (higher degree by research). Masters coursework degrees are explicitly excluded.
Full-time: up to 2 years of support, with no minimum published. Part-time: up to 4 years.
Stipend rate for part-time students is 50% of the full-time rate offered by the university.
Part-time RTP stipends are taxable; full-time RTP stipends are considered tax exempt provided the additional ATO criteria are met.
phd: Research doctorate degrees only (higher degree by research).
Full-time: minimum 3 years, maximum 4 years. Part-time: minimum 6 years, maximum 8 years.

Support must be provided for at least 3 years and up to 4 years full-time; these durations are doubled for part-time students. Eligible universities have discretion to award any period within these ranges and cannot provide extensions beyond the maximum.

The maximum period of support is calculated from the student's HDR course commencement date, which may or may not have occurred at a previous university and may or may not have been supported through the RTP. Support is not reset or extended on transfer to a different university.
Stipend rate for part-time students is 50% of the full-time rate offered by the university.

host_requirements: The university must be an eligible higher education provider receiving research block grants (published as a separate list by the Department of Education).
The university must administer RTP scholarships itself, including the application, selection and offer processes and deadlines.
The university must publish an RTP scholarship policy on its webpage detailing its application, selection and offer process.

The university must clearly distinguish, in all communications about student selection (including websites and direct communications), between the student eligibility criteria specified by the Guidelines and any additional selection criteria it sets.
The university must provide information regarding suspensions of RTP scholarships in its RTP scholarship policy.
The university must provide a stipend rate at least equal to the base full-time RTP stipend rate and no more than the maximum full-time RTP stipend rate, using RTP funding.
The university must inform students of the estimated value of each type of RTP scholarship support awarded in the RTP offer letter.
The university must include in its RTP scholarship policy the circumstances in which it will not approve a student to undertake work outside their HDR, including any restrictions on hours worked.
The university must include information on both outgoing and incoming transfers of RTP scholarships in its RTP scholarship policy.
In administering RTP scholarships a university may only spend up to 10% of its RTP funding per grant year on providing scholarships to international students.
official.selection_notes: Selection is institutional, not Commonwealth. Published: 'Universities have the discretion to award RTP scholarships as a result of a competitive selection process, the nature of which is determined by the university.' In determining its selection process a university may take into consideration previous study, relevant work experience, research publications, referee reports and other research experience, and may give priority to students undertaking research in a particular discipline or emerging area of research strength, students who achieved specific marks in their previous degree(s), students undertaking a research degree for the first time, or students studying on campus and/or in person. No Commonwealth assessment rubric, score or interview requirement is published. The Guidelines deliberately place only a floor under eligibility (for example, first class honours is not required, and holding a research degree from an overseas university, having previously completed an HDR, or having withdrawn from a previous RTP are not bars), leaving the rest to the provider's published policy.
application_steps: Identify eligible Australian higher education providers (the Department of Education publishes the list of higher education providers eligible for research block grants).
Read the chosen university's published RTP scholarship policy, which must detail its application, selection and offer process.
Contact the university's postgraduate research office directly to discuss how to apply and whether RTP is available to international students.
Check the university's internal deadline - the university sets it and the Commonwealth publishes none.
Apply through the university according to its published process (including any English language or IELTS requirement the university sets).
If offered, read the RTP offer letter, which must state the estimated value of each type of support awarded (fees offset, stipend, allowances).
On acceptance, acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in research publications using the required wording and the RTP DOI, and add the DOI to your ORCID profile if you have one.
applicant_submission_route: Student -> chosen eligible Australian university (postgraduate research office / its RTP scholarship application process). The student applies at the university level; RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education.
official.application_portal: No Commonwealth portal. Each eligible Australian university runs its own application process, which must be detailed in its RTP scholarship policy published on the university's webpage.
timeline_rules: RTP base and maximum stipend rates are indexed each year, effective from 1 January; the base and maximum rates for the following year are announced by 1 October each year.

Published full-time stipend rates (AUD per year): 2025 - base 33,511, maximum 52,352; 2026 - base 34,315, maximum 53,608; 2027 - base 35,550, maximum 55,537. The announced rates apply to all RTP stipend payments made in the relevant year, not only to new recipients.

Period of support: research doctorate full-time minimum 3 years / maximum 4 years; research doctorate part-time minimum 6 years / maximum 8 years; research masters full-time up to 2 years; research masters part-time up to 4 years.

A student's period of support will not be increased for periods of paid recreation leave or personal leave approved by the provider, but will be increased by the length of any RTP Scholarship Suspension, additional paid personal leave, paid parental leave, paid partner leave, or paid family and domestic violence leave approved by the provider.

Industry internship weighting: the written internship agreement must be made within 18 months of course commencement for a full-time student or within 36 months for a part-time student, extended by any HDR period of suspension in the first 18 months or any increase to the period of support.

From 3 December 2025 the Higher Education Support (Commonwealth Scholarships) Guidelines 2025 apply, replacing the Commonwealth Scholarships Guidelines (Research) 2017. The former rule that a student must not receive income from another source related to the course of study and greater than 75% of the RTP stipend rate was removed with the new Guidelines.
The RTP digital object identifier is doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220.

official_contacts.general: Department of Education research block grants enquiries. Additional routes published: your university's postgraduate research office or scholarship office; Services Australia for the Child Care Subsidy; the Department of Home Affairs for visa questions.

official_application_route: Direct to the chosen eligible Australian university - contact its postgraduate research office and apply under the process in its published RTP scholarship policy. RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education.
A student may apply to more than one university, or more than once at the same university; the provider decides the process.

Transfers: a student may transfer from one eligible Australian university to another subject to the new university accepting them and agreeing to continuation; there is no transfer of funding between universities and the new university must have sufficient RTP funds available.

important_advice_for_students: There is no Commonwealth application and no Commonwealth deadline. Everything - application, selection, deadline, documents, English test - is set by the university, and it must publish that in its RTP scholarship policy. Read the policy before you spend anything on applications.

As an international student you are eligible, but your university may only spend up to 10% of its RTP funding per grant year on international students. Ask the postgraduate research office directly whether any RTP places are available to internationals before you invest in a research proposal.

Check the exact combination you are being offered. A university may give you a fees offset only, stipend only, allowance only, or a combination, and the fee offset amount varies by university and research area. The offer letter must state the estimated value of each component.

Budget on the range, not a number. The stipend must be at least the base full-time rate and no more than the maximum: for 2027 that is AUD 35,550 to AUD 55,537 per year; 2026 was AUD 34,315 to AUD 53,608. Part-time is 50% of whatever the university offers and is taxable, whereas full-time stipends are tax exempt if you meet the ATO criteria.
If you are an international student, ask whether an OSHC allowance is included. It is listed as a valid allowance use, but it is not automatic.

Do not assume a scholarship you must not combine still blocks you. The old rule barring other income related to the course of study above 75% of the stipend was removed on 3 December 2025. But if you already hold a Commonwealth award for HDR tuition fees, that bars an RTP fees offset - so check before you accept a second offer.

Plan your period of support carefully. It is counted from your HDR commencement date, including any time done at a previous university, and it is not reset if you transfer. Support cannot be extended beyond the maximum (4 years FT doctorate, 8 years PT doctorate, 2 years FT masters, 4 years PT masters).
Check whether your provider restricts paid work. The provider must publish the circumstances in which it will not let you work outside your HDR, including any hours cap.
You will have to acknowledge the Commonwealth in publications, and add the RTP DOI to your ORCID profile if you have one.

referee_tracking.role: Referee reports - at the provider's discretion, not a Commonwealth requirement
referee_tracking.instructions: The Commonwealth Guidelines do not name a required number of referees. FAQ 4 and FAQ 8 both state only that 'in determining its selection process for RTP scholarship, a university may consider previous study, relevant work experience, research publications, referee reports, and other factors'. The number of referees, who may be contacted, and the form of the report are set in the university's RTP scholarship policy and its HDR admission requirements. Check both, and contact referees early - academic referees can be slow.

post_award_requirements: Acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in research publications using the required wording: 'This research was supported by the Commonwealth through an Australian Government Research Training Program Scholarship [DOI: https://doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220] .' This applies to recipients of an RTP fees offset, stipend or allowance.
Include the RTP DOI in your ORCID profile if you already have one (the Funding section is described as appropriate). There is no requirement to create an ORCID profile if you do not have one.
Meet the provider's rules on work outside your HDR, which the provider must publish in its RTP scholarship policy.
Follow the provider's published suspension process; the provider must publish how suspensions operate.

Accept the provider's conditions on paid recreation leave, personal leave, additional personal leave, parental leave, partner leave and family and domestic violence leave, and note which of these extend the period of support.
Maintain enrolment and progress in the HDR; the provider administers the scholarship.
questions_to_ask_host: Do you offer RTP to international students this year, and how many places are left under your 10% cap?
Which combination will I receive - fees offset, stipend, allowances - and what is the estimated value of each, as stated in my offer letter?
What stipend rate will I be paid, and is it the base rate or above? Will the rate be re-indexed each 1 January?
Will the award be full-time or part-time, and does a part-time load halve the stipend?
Is an OSHC allowance included for me and my dependants, and is a relocation allowance available?
What is your internal closing date, and what documents, formats and referee reports do you require?
What English language or IELTS requirement applies to international applicants in your RTP process?
What restrictions do you place on paid work, and do I need approval before taking any work?
What is your policy on suspending the scholarship, and on transferring to another university without resetting my period of support?
How does the RTP industry internship weighting work for my research doctorate, and what is the deadline for the written internship agreement?
common_rejection_risks: Missing the university's internal deadline - the Commonwealth publishes none, so all timing risk sits with the provider.
Applying for a coursework degree (bachelor or masters coursework) instead of a research degree.
Applying for an HDR at an overseas university rather than an eligible Australian provider.
The provider having no international-student RTP places available under its 10% cap.
Holding another Commonwealth award or scholarship for HDR tuition fees, which bars an RTP fees offset.

Missing the provider's additional selection criteria - first class honours is not required by the Guidelines, but marks, discipline, first-time-research status and on-campus study are all things providers publish as priorities.
Failing the provider's English language or IELTS requirement.
Assuming the maximum stipend rate. The provider sets a rate within the base-to-maximum band.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any part of the HDR tuition fee not covered by the fees offset - the offset must fully cover applicable HDR fees, but the student must check the estimated value in the offer letter because it varies by university and research area.
Living costs above the stipend actually offered. The stipend is a band, not a fixed amount.

Everything not covered by an allowance: the published allowance examples are relocation, thesis printing, academic publication and OSHC. Books, equipment, conference travel and living-cost shortfalls are not named as covered.
Living costs for dependants beyond any OSHC allowance.
For part-time students, the difference between 100% and 50% of the full-time rate, and the tax payable on the part-time stipend.
Unpaid research-related costs if the provider offers fees offset only with no stipend and no allowances.
document_audit: The Commonwealth publishes no RTP document list for students. Required documents are those of the university's RTP scholarship application process and its HDR admission requirements, published in the university's RTP scholarship policy.
No file size limits, accepted file types, translation rules, date-of-issue rules or signature rules are published centrally. document_format_rules is therefore deliberately empty.

What is certain from the published sources: referee reports may be required (the provider's discretion); the offer letter must state the estimated value of each type of support; if an industry internship weighting is being claimed, the written agreement between student, provider and research end-user must be in place within the published 18-month (full-time) or 36-month (part-time) window.

For international students, the Australian visa application's funding section is a separate Department of Home Affairs matter; both the Department of Home Affairs and the university's postgraduate research office may assist.

alerts.message: New base and maximum RTP stipend rates for the following year are announced (effective 1 January). The new rates apply to all RTP stipend payments made in that year, not only to new recipients.
Open the chosen university's RTP scholarship policy. The Commonwealth application, selection criteria, deadline, documents and English requirement are all in that document.
Check the offer letter lists the estimated value of each support type, and check you are not in receipt of another Commonwealth award for HDR tuition fees.
Track your period of support from the HDR commencement date. It is not reset by a transfer and cannot be extended beyond the maximum.
Include the required acknowledgement sentence and the RTP DOI 10.82133/C42F-K220, and add it to your ORCID profile if you have one.

official.description: The Monash International Leadership Scholarship pays 100% of course fees for the duration of an undergraduate degree, with only four awarded per year. It is open to international students from all countries who have received a full, unconditional Monash course offer and intend to enrol full-time at a Monash campus in Australia, and requires no application because eligibility is assessed automatically. Recipients must maintain a Weighted Average Mark of 70 each semester, join the Campus Ambassador Program from their second semester, and provide a student profile for Monash marketing use. The award explicitly excludes overseas student health cover, accommodation and living costs.

purpose: The Humphrey Fellowship, a Fulbright exchange, advances American interests by bringing influential professionals from priority countries to the United States to build strategic partnerships that advance shared interests and support U.S. foreign policy goals. Through graduate-level study and professional experiences at U.S. host universities and organizations, Humphrey Fellows gain practical insight into how American policies are developed and implemented, working alongside U.S. experts in their fields.

The Humphrey Fellowship Program, a Fulbright Exchange, cultivates relationships between government officials in targeted countries and the United States, creating a global network of U.S.-trained leaders who cooperate with the United States in areas such as combatting illicit drug trafficking, economic and trade partnerships, emerging technologies, law, and space governance.

Leadership development that builds lasting ties in critical fields between Americans and their professional counterparts overseas; a personalized academic experience at more than 7 U.S. higher education institutions; a network of over 7,000 alumni.

Founded in 1978 to honour the late Senator and Vice President Hubert H. Humphrey. In 1979 the first Humphrey Fellows arrived in the United States, welcoming 27 mid-career professionals from 24 countries to 11 U.S. universities.
sdg_requirement_details: No Sustainable Development Goal requirement is published. Work is organised instead by four published impact areas: Human & Institutional Capacity (Economic Development; Finance and Banking; Public Policy Analysis and Public Administration; Technology Policy and Management); Rights & Freedoms (Communications/Journalism; Law and Human Rights); Sustainable Lands (Agricultural and Rural Development; Natural Resources, Sustainability, and Environmental Policy; Urban and Regional Planning); Thriving Communities (Public Health Policy and Management; Substance Abuse Education, Treatment and Prevention; Educational Administration, Planning, and Policy).

important_advice_for_students: You cannot download this application. The programme publishes no application form or central portal; you must go to the U.S. Embassy (Public Affairs Section) or Binational Fulbright Commission in your own country.

Start with your country's post early. Deadlines vary by country and are set locally, but every post has to submit its nominations to Washington by mid-September. If you discover the process in October you have already missed the cycle.
Check the country eligibility list before anything else. The programme is limited to targeted/priority countries.
Five years of full-time professional experience is the hard floor, and part-time work alone may not count - the FAQ says candidates with only part-time work experience may not be considered eligible.

The US-experience rule is easy to trip over. More than three years cumulatively in the US makes you ineligible unless you have been back home and employed at a professional level of responsibility for at least four years.

You do not get a degree, and you do not choose your university. It is a ten-month non-degree programme and you are assigned to one of 7 host universities in a group of 13-15 based on your field. If you need a credential, this is the wrong award.

Budget the family question carefully. There is no additional maintenance allowance for dependants. You personally must show proof of financial support, adequate insurance meeting State Department requirements, and child care plans before J-2 visas for dependants can even be applied for. And not all countries permit dependants at all.

The programme is described as rigorous and unlike graduate study with regular hours, and Fellows spend considerable time away from the host campus. Plan your professional obligations at home accordingly.
If TOEFL is your only English evidence, that is not a bar by itself - IELTS or the Duolingo English Test can be used for all candidates - but eligibility questions go to your Embassy or Commission.

purpose: The Wien International Scholarship Program (WISP) at Brandeis University, established in 1958, is a first-of-its-kind program bringing undergraduate students from every corner of the globe to campus and engaging the entire community to be active global citizens.

The Wien Scholarship meets the full demonstrated financial need of each recipient, based on a complete review of financial documentation. It is awarded to exceptional international applicants who demonstrate strong academic achievement and extracurricular or community involvement.

Since its inception the programme has brought over 894 scholars from 115 countries to Brandeis; its graduates continue to be committed to Brandeis University and to improving the world. Wien Scholars are identified not only by academic achievement but by their contributions inside and outside the classroom prior to, during and after their years at Brandeis.

important_advice_for_students: There is no separate Wien application and no nominating partner. Brandeis states plainly that it does not partner with any external individuals or organizations for selection. Understand what you are applying for: a need-based award that meets your full demonstrated financial need as Brandeis calculates it, not a fixed sum. Ask Brandeis's financial aid office what their cost of attendance and net price calculation produces for your case before you compare this against another offer.

Get your financial documentation right the first time. The amount depends on a complete review of financial documentation. If you are seeking financial aid, that means a completed CSS Profile; if you are not, it means the Certification of Finances for International Students through DEISConnect. Either way you need employer earnings statements, bank or financial institution certifications, or tax returns showing the family's first-year contribution.

Do the English test early, or use the exemption. TOEFL iBT, IELTS, DET or Cambridge (C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency) are accepted. Four or more years in a high school where the full curriculum is in English lets you request a waiver in DEISConnect after applying, and United World College applicants are exempt outright.
Note the DET rule: Duolingo English Test scores must come straight from the testing agency. Scanned copies are fine for TOEFL, IELTS and Cambridge only.
Senior midyear grades are required for Regular Decision applicants and often do not exist until late January or early February - build the application around that if you choose Regular Decision.

Admissions interviews at Brandeis are by invitation only. If you want an interview, book InitialView or Vericant early: the record-and-submit deadlines are 15 November for Early Decision I and 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision.

Plan on the award being renewable but not permanent. Brandeis publishes renewal for up to eight semesters provided renewal requirements are met, and the amount stays the same throughout - but it does not publish what those renewal requirements are.

Do not falsify or massage anything. Brandeis denies admission for falsified materials and can withdraw the offer, withdraw you from the University, or revoke a conferred degree if falsification surfaces later.

Brandeis does not publish a letter format, word limit, or whether referees are contacted directly; recommendations are submitted through the application as per Brandeis's instructions and Brandeis advises contacting your college counsellor or teachers to confirm they were sent.

Complete financial documentation honestly and, if circumstances change, expect your demonstrated need to be recalculated since the award is set from a complete review of financial documentation.

Observe the credential verification policy: falsified or misleading materials can lead to denial of admission, withdrawal of the admission offer, withdrawal from the University, or revocation of a degree.

purpose: Clark University offers a variety of merit-based scholarships. Consideration is given to students who have demonstrated exceptional academic performance and personal qualities during their secondary school years.
Through generous need-based aid and merit scholarships, we seek to make a Clark education affordable for every student regardless of income level.
Published institutional aid statistics: 99% of first-year students receive aid; 98% of all aid awarded are grants that do not have to be repaid.
official.funding_amount: No single named scholarship amount applies - Clark publishes a mix of need-dependent and need-independent figures. Published figures as at 2026-10-01: (1) Average financial aid package USD 50,755 (Undergraduate Admissions 'Cost and Financial Aid' page) / USD 49,545 (Office of Financial Assistance 'Apply for financial aid' page) - the two official pages publish different figures for the same statistic and neither states a year or population; (2) Presidential Scholarship - covers the full costs of tuition plus on-campus housing and meals for the four years of undergraduate study, with recipients responsible for additional costs totalling approximately USD 12,000-15,000 per year; (3) Davis United World College Scholars Program - need-based grant of up to USD 15,000 per year from the Shelby Davis family; (4) International students - 'Typically, international students pay around $40,000 per year after considering scholarships and aid. Our total cost of attendance is approximately $85,000 per year'; (5) Clark's published 2026-2027 cost of attendance: Tuition USD 62,070; Room (standard double) USD 8,580; Board (standard plan) USD 5,780; Student Activity & Programming Fee USD 460; Orientation Fee USD 400; Health and Wellness Fee USD 680; Total billed charges USD 77,970; Transportation allowance USD 250; Books (estimated) USD 900; Miscellaneous (estimated) USD 800; Health Insurance USD 2,833; Total Estimated Costs USD 82,753.
official.tuition_coverage: Partial and conditional. Merit scholarships are awarded on academic merit without regard to need, and no tuition-only waiver mechanism is published. The top award, the Presidential Scholarship, 'covers the full costs of tuition, as well as on-campus housing and meals, for the four years of undergraduate study' - but Clark states that recipients 'are responsible for additional costs totaling approximately $12,000-$15,000 per year'. For other international applicants Clark states explicitly that while it provides merit and need-based aid, 'it may not cover all educational expenses', and that because resources are limited 'we can't offer admission to international students who require full funding.'
official.tuition_rule: There is no tuition-waiver instrument. Aid works in three published channels. (1) Merit: 'Merit scholarship decisions are made solely based on information presented in the admission application without consideration of financial need', and admitted students who receive a merit-based scholarship are notified at the time of admission. (2) Need-based: offered based on family financial circumstances as institutional or government grants that do not need to be repaid, or federal loans; students must reapply annually. (3) External/private: if you receive a private scholarship you must inform the Clark University Office of Financial Assistance in writing, and private scholarships are counted as part of your aid package rather than added on top. A Federal Work-Study award, where the student qualifies, is included in the financial aid offer letter.
official.home_tuition_rule: Not published. Clark publishes nothing about fees at, or continuation of study at, the applicant's previous school.
official.host_institution_fee: The host institution is Clark University and the published fees are its own: Student Activity & Programming Fee USD 460, Orientation Fee USD 400, Health and Wellness Fee USD 680 (2026-2027), plus estimated Books USD 900, Miscellaneous USD 800, Transportation allowance USD 250 and Health Insurance USD 2,833. In Massachusetts State Law terms, Clark requires all matriculated full-time and three-quarter-time students to participate in the Student Health Insurance Plan unless proof of comprehensive comparable coverage under a policy filed and approved in the U.S. is provided. Which of these fees any individual merit or need-based award covers is not published.
official.tax_status: Not published. Clark publishes no tax treatment for merit or need-based awards paid to an F-1 student.

For students in 6-3-3 systems (for example China), a middle school transcript showing results from at least the final/third year (US equivalent of 9th grade) is required in addition to the first two years of the three-year secondary school.
Transcripts should be submitted through the Common Application or Coalition Application (preferred), or emailed directly to intadmissions@clarku.edu.

Two recommendation letters are required - one from a school counselor and one from a teacher. Where no school counselor or university advisor exists, submit letters from two academic teachers. official.selection_notes: Merit: consideration is automatic for all applicants, decisions are made solely on the admission application without consideration of financial need, and admitted recipients are notified at the time of admission. Presidential Scholarship: awarded to approximately five exceptional students annually per the Undergraduate Admissions page and to 3-5 students annually per the International Students page - the two official pages differ; there is no separate application process; all admitted students are considered by the scholarship committee based on the strength of the admissions application; finalists are selected and invited to interview. Need-based: assessed from the CSS Profile. Admissions: need-aware, and an application may be denied where indicated need exceeds what Clark can offer. No scoring rubric, GPA threshold or weighting between academic performance and personal qualities is published.

Submit an official English proficiency score report (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Pearson PTE) if English is not your native language.

File the CSS Profile with your application by the admissions deadline if you want to be considered for a need-based award. Apply for financial aid early - Clark states the FAFSA and any other required financial aid materials are due by the same deadlines as the admission application.

Complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form on the applicant status portal (all international students must).

Optionally schedule an interview - in person, virtual, via InitialView or Vericant, or by emailing intadmissions@clarku.edu to request a virtual slot. For international students the interview can also serve as a supplementary measurement of English proficiency.

official_application_route: 1. Submit the Common Application or Coalition Application with Scoir to Clark University Undergraduate Admissions by the round's deadline (Nov 1 for Early Decision I / Early Action; Jan 15 for Early Decision II / Regular Decision).
2. Send transcripts (last three years, in English) and two recommendation letters (school counselor and teacher, or two academic teachers) through the application or to intadmissions@clarku.edu.

common_rejection_risks: Applying as an international student who needs full funding - Clark states it cannot offer admission in that case. This is a hard institutional limit, not a competitiveness judgement.
Indicating a financial need greater than Clark can offer. The admissions process is need-aware and the application may be denied on that basis.
Missing the CSS Profile deadline - the CSS Profile must be filed by the admissions deadline, so a late filing forfeits need-based consideration entirely.

Forgetting the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form, which all international students must complete and which only becomes available after applying.
Submitting only two years of educational data. Clark cannot review an application with only two years of credentials, and 6-3-3 systems need an extra middle school year.
Sending the Duolingo English Test score as a screenshot or scan - it must come directly from the Duolingo portal.
Non-English documents with no certified translation.
Missing an optional-looking deadline that is not optional, such as senior-year records that do not yet exist in your system.
Assuming a Presidential Scholarship means the whole cost - even that award leaves approximately USD 12,000-15,000 per year payable by the recipient.
Assuming a private scholarship will be added on top of Clark's package - it must be declared and is counted within it, and an undeclared external award can change your package.
Early Decision applicants who are admitted but then enrol elsewhere, breaching a binding agreement.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Approximately USD 40,000 per year for a typical international student after scholarships and aid, against a total cost of attendance of approximately USD 85,000 per year.
For a Presidential Scholarship recipient, approximately USD 12,000-15,000 per year in additional costs beyond tuition, on-campus housing and meals.
Student Activity & Programming Fee (USD 460), Orientation Fee (USD 400) and Health and Wellness Fee (USD 680) for 2026-2027 - Clark does not publish which awards cover these.
Estimated books (USD 900), miscellaneous expenses (USD 800) and a transportation allowance (USD 250).
Health Insurance (USD 2,833 in the 2026-2027 published cost) unless you can evidence comprehensive comparable coverage under a policy filed and approved in the U.S.
Anything beyond Clark's published aid capacity, which is why an applicant who needs full funding cannot be admitted at all.
Cost of third-party interview services (InitialView or Vericant) if you choose to use one.

Named sponsors include the Ramon Areces Foundation (all applicants to the Economics and Financial Economics programmes) and the Unicredit Foundation (one full scholarship for Economics or Finance), each covering 100% of tuition, with further sponsors providing full or partial waivers to all Master's applicants. Applications open in October for the following academic year and the first admissions round closes 15 January, with applications completed before that date considered for all funding.
official.program_type: University and sponsor-funded master's scholarships and tuition waivers (merit-based)
official.coverage: Named scholarships cover 100% of tuition fees, and some additional stipend depending on the scholarship; other sponsors provide full or partial tuition waivers. Living costs, travel and insurance are not mentioned as covered.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply in the first round and get a complete file in before 15 January if you want to be considered for all funding
Register in the BSE application system early, since you need the account to start
Prepare a mathematics-heavy statement of purpose that explains your recent mathematical background through courses, research or practical applications
Brief your two referees in advance - letters from professors are strongly preferred, and BSE contacts referees by email after you submit
Arrange the EUR 100 application fee (credit card or Flywire) as part of your submission
Have your language score ready (TOEFL 90, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 120 or Cambridge 180), or wait until you can provide it
Add a GRE score if you are applying to the PhD Economics Track
common_rejection_risks: Missing 15 January, which limits you to whatever funding is left
An incomplete application because one or both reference letters were never uploaded - the application is not considered complete until both arrive
A weak quantitative background, which BSE calls a key admission criterion alongside academic record and reference letter
Missing the mathematics explanation in the statement of purpose, which BSE calls essential
Applying without a language certificate
Assuming admission guarantees funding - fulfilment of application requirements does not guarantee admission, and aid is merit-based
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Barcelona, which no published award states it covers
Travel and health insurance
Any portion of tuition not covered by a named scholarship or waiver
document_audit: Undergraduate diploma or degree-completion certification, or the signed declaration plus provisional transcript
Official final undergraduate transcript
Sworn translation if not in English, Spanish, Catalan, French, Italian or Portuguese
CV of no more than 2 pages
Statement of purpose
English language certificate at the published level
Passport copy
Both signed reference letters uploaded by the referees themselves

alerts.message: About 20% of admitted students are non-economists, but strong quantitative skills are essential whatever your background.
Your decision comes in roughly 5 weeks instead of mid-February, and you are considered only for any funding still available.

alerts.trigger: You rely on a language test you do not yet have
alerts.message: BSE advises waiting to apply until you can provide the certificate, rather than applying without it.

submission_workflow: Choose up to 3 BSE Master's programs
Create your account in the BSE application system
Complete the application questions, including finance and scholarship details and both referees' details
Upload transcripts, diploma or declaration, CV, statement of purpose, language certificate and passport
Ask both referees to upload their signed letters directly, and remind them to watch for BSE's email
Pay the EUR 100 application fee by credit card or Flywire
Submit before 15 January to be eligible for all funding opportunities

official.description: IE University offers three families of master's financial aid. Direct Awards are merit-based and granted automatically upon admission with no separate financial aid application. IE Awards cover between 10% and 40% of tuition fees, require a financial aid application, and are assessed on merit and financial need. IE Foundation Scholarships are offered with partner organisations and generous donors and may cover up to 100% of tuition and living costs.

The IE Financial Aid Committee will not reconsider a disappointing outcome unless you can show significant and unexpected changes in your financial situation, and only by the programme start date.
If you also hold a Direct Award, you may still apply for additional financial aid.

official.description: Esade's Scholarship Program funds academically excellent students with limited financial resources. MSc and MBA Talent Scholarships (published as Esade Need-based Scholarships) cover 50% to 85% of the programme tuition fee and are assessed on talent and financial need. Esade also runs Excellence Awards, which are talent-only, range from 10% to 50% of MSc tuition, and are limited to one award per candidate. Living costs are handled separately through Lodging, Living, Exchange and SUD grants.
purpose: The Esade community is entirely committed to supporting talent and diversity. Esade believes that having that talent and diversity in their classrooms is fundamental to be able to enrich students' educational experience, providing them with ever greater learning opportunities and favoring progress and social justice at the same time.
To help support and develop the best talent, Esade strives to attract the most outstanding students, regardless of their financial situations, origins, cultural backgrounds and religious beliefs.

Esade's Scholarship Program offers talented students with excellent academic track records from diverse socio-economic backgrounds the opportunity to study at Esade. All Esade scholarships are possible thanks to the generosity of its community, so that academically excellent students with limited financial resources can study at Esade.

Talent Scholarships cover between 60% and 100% of recipients' tuition fees for their entire undergraduate or double-degree programs, all based on the individual candidates' academic results and their financial need.

When a percentage differs by programme â€” Princesa de Girona at up to 50% for MSc and up to 75% for MBA â€” both are recorded rather than averaged or reconciled.
verification.source_freshness_rule: Esade's financing pages are rebuilt each intake and deliberately carry mixed years: fee tables are published ahead (2027-2028) while award deadlines refer to the current intake (2026). Any deadline, fee or percentage must be matched to the correct intake label before use, and re-checked annually. The Scholarship Program impact statistics are explicitly labelled 2022-2023 and should not be presented as current-year figures.

application_readiness_checklist: Be on a full-time PhD at NTU. NPGS is not available for Master's programmes.
Have, or be on track for, an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent â€” if your degree is unfinished, get written confirmation from your university now, because this is a hard gate.
Line up a supervisor before you submit. It is highly recommended; if you cannot, NTU will appoint one based on your research interests, but you lose control of that match.
Assemble resume, educational certificates and transcripts, test scores and recommendation letters per the Research Programmes Admission Guide 'How to Apply â€“ Supporting Documents' list.
Check every test score's date: scores must be within 5 years or less from the date of your application.
If your prior study was in English and you want a test waiver, request a medium-of-instruction letter from your home university.
Apply in the October/November to December window and tick interest in the 'NTU Scholarship' in the application â€” there is no separate scholarship form.
Plan for the final interview at university level; outcomes land roughly 3 to 6 weeks after it.
Have a Singapore bank account ready and update your details in GSLink by the 15th of the semester commencement month.
important_advice_for_students: There is no bond. NTU states plainly that there is no bond attached to the scholarship, so you are not locked into returning to your home country.
Do not read 'priority will be given for campus accommodation' as free housing. It is a queue preference; you still need to budget for rent, and priority does not guarantee a place.
Budget in Singapore dollars and by citizenship tier. Your stipend is S$5,300 (Citizen), S$4,800 (PR) or S$4,300 (International), and only Citizens get the CPF contribution on top.
Renewal is not automatic in name: it is renewable 'subject to good progress', up to 4 years, and the school also weighs availability of research funding. Keep your progress reports clean.
As an International Student you will be required to do teaching or laboratory supervision under the Graduate Assistantship Programme. Factor that workload into your research time.
NTU reserves the right to vary the stipend at any time and states that coverage and award terms are subject to change â€” do not build a fixed budget on today's figure.
If you are an existing student on a higher stipend rate, NTU says your stipend remains the same; the revised rates apply from January 2026.
The conference allowance is capped and runs on a financial-year basis (April to March), so plan conference travel against the S$5,000 cap and the April-to-March window.
You do not need a separate scholarship application. The single most common administrative mistake is simply forgetting to indicate the 'NTU Scholarship' in the programme application.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a Master's programme â€” NPGS is only for PhD.
Not holding, and not being able to evidence being on track for, an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent.
Failing to supply the official university documentation confirming on-track status when the undergraduate degree is incomplete.
Missing the October/November to December application window, or submitting before the period for the academic year is announced.
Submitting an incomplete application â€” consideration happens on submission of a complete application within the period.
Forgetting to indicate interest in the 'NTU Scholarship' in the programme application.
Submitting GRE/GMAT scores older than 5 years from the application date.
Requesting a test waiver without the home university medium-of-instruction letter.
Not attending or not preparing for the final interview at university level.
Failing to update GSLink bank details by the 15th of the semester commencement month, which delays stipend payment.
Applying for the wrong NTU entity â€” NIE runs a separately announced application period.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation and rent â€” the award gives only priority for campus accommodation; it does not pay for housing.
Airfare to Singapore and any relocation cost â€” no travel or relocation allowance is published.
Anything beyond the S$5,000 per financial year Overseas Conference Allowance cap.
Personal, medical and day-to-day living costs above what the monthly stipend and the book, IT and thesis allowances cover.
Costs arising if the award is not renewed: renewal is subject to good progress and to the school's determination and availability of research funding, so plan for an unpaid final period.

important_advice_for_students: There is no separate fellowship application form at UGC. The only thing you apply for is the qualifying test. The fellowship follows from the result plus an institutional registration.

The two-year clock is the real deadline and the institution holds it, not you. UGC says registration for the M.Phil/PhD is made by the University/Institution/College within two years of the declaration of result, issue of the award letter, or joining the fellowship. Chase your institution in writing.

Your qualifying category is worth as much as your score. NTA is explicit that the 'appointment as Assistant Professor and admission to Ph.D.' category does not carry the JRF award, and 'admission to Ph.D. only' does not carry either.
Do not budget the fellowship as covering tuition. UGC's published financial assistance is the monthly fellowship plus a contingency allowance, with no mention of fee payment.

Note the two-tier contingency. Humanities and Social Sciences scholars get Contingency A (Rs. 10,000 pa as JRF, Rs. 20,500 pa as SRF); Science scholars get Contingency B (Rs. 12,000 pa as JRF, Rs. 25,000 pa as SRF). Science scholars receive more.
Plan for the step-up at 2 years: your rate rises from Rs. 37,000 to Rs. 42,000 and your contingency also steps up, so year three onwards is better than years one and two.

If you are a foreign national, resolve your eligibility before anything else. NTA frames UGC-NET as determining 'the eligibility of Indian nationals' for the JRF award, and the UGC scheme page publishes no foreign-national provision. Do not assume you can sit the test and claim the fellowship.

Assuming a Research Associateship is a separate UGC scheme that can be applied for directly â€” UGC's Student Corner lists only two fellowships and does not publish an RA scheme page.

official.description: The TWAS-CSIR Postgraduate Fellowship Programme, run jointly by India's Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and UNESCO-TWAS, funds foreign scholars from developing countries to pursue research toward a PhD in CSIR laboratories and institutes in India. It is restricted to researchers aged 35 or under on 31 December of the application year, nationals of developing countries other than India who hold no residency visa in India or a developed country, holders of an MSc who are employed with a research assignment at home, and who can secure an official acceptance letter from a CSIR host. The fellowship pays a monthly stipend for living costs, food and health insurance plus subsidised accommodation, for up to 4 years full-time or 6 months to 3 years as a sandwich fellowship. The 2026 call closed on 3 June 2026 after an extension from 20 May.

official.description: The Netaji Subhas - ICAR International Fellowship (NS-ICAR IF) funds a three-year Ph.D. in agriculture and allied sciences in identified priority areas, for both Indian candidates studying abroad and overseas candidates studying at Indian Agricultural Universities in the ICAR-AU system. Thirty fellowships are available each year. The award pays a monthly stipend plus a contingent and preparatory lump sum and provides a to-and-fro economy class air ticket, but host institution fees, medical insurance and medical fitness are all paid by the fellow.
purpose: In its continued efforts towards enhancing and sustaining the standards, quality and relevance of higher agricultural education in the country, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has instituted International Fellowships with dual purpose of (i) human resource development in cutting edge technologies, and (ii) demonstrating the strength of Indian agricultural system abroad.

The objective is to develop competent human resource that are trained in the identified best laboratories in the world (for Indian candidates) and similarly expose overseas candidates to the best Indian Agricultural Universities (AUs) in the ICAR-AU system (comprising of State Agricultural Universities, Central Agricultural University Imphal, ICAR-Deemed Universities, Allahabad Agricultural Institute-DU, Central Universities having agricultural faculty) for creating a pool of scientist-envoys for enhanced future co-operation.

The NS-ICAR IFs are available to support Indian/overseas nationals for pursuing doctoral degree in agriculture and allied sciences, in the identified priority areas, to the Indian candidates for study abroad in the identified overseas Universities/Institutions having strong research and teaching capabilities, and to overseas candidates for study in the best Indian AUs in the ICAR-AUs system.
The Netaji Subhas-ICAR International Fellowships are available in frontier areas of Agriculture and allied sciences at the recognized agricultural universities/institutions in India and abroad.
study_type: Doctoral (Ph.D.) research in agriculture and allied sciences
Must be within the Council's identified priority areas of research, which are notified one year in advance
Priority areas span Crop Sciences, Horticulture, Biotechnology and nanotechnology, Animal Sciences, Natural Resource Management, Agricultural Engineering and Fisheries

official.duration: Three years. "The NS-ICAR IFs are available to Indian candidates as well as overseas candidates for a period of three years." The tenure of fellowship will not be extended in any case, in so far as the Council support is concerned. If the fellow is not able to complete the degree during this period, he/she will use his/her own resources for completing the degree.
official.application_cycle: Annual. "Applications for NS-ICAR IFs will be invited on annual basis through announcements published in Indian national newspapers and the notification on ICAR website 'http://www.icar.org.in'. Indian diplomatic missions in foreign countries will also be informed through e-mails." The Council will identify and announce the priority areas of research and the list of institutions for admission one year in advance. For the year 2026, thirty (30) fellowships for a duration of three years are available, split between Indian and overseas candidates according to the availability of good candidates in the identified priority areas.

official.selection_notes: Candidates are evaluated on a parameters/weighted scale covering the relevance of the area of study, the proposed research plan, academic records, achievements and past work experience. Selection is then made on the basis of the evaluation score and a subsequent interview by a Selection Committee constituted by the Council and duly empowered to judge the suitability of the candidate with regard to the importance of the area of study and the proposed research plan. The Committee may also decide to conduct a telephonic/teleconferencing interview, and the overseas candidates may even be interviewed by experts as identified by the Council who may be based in their home country. The two referees may be directly contacted by the Council for comments in the prescribed format on the candidature. At the time of interview the applicants must furnish a letter of acceptance for their admission in the respective degree programme at the University. The allocation of the thirty fellowships between Indian and overseas candidates depends on the availability of good candidates in the identified priority areas. The Secretary, ICAR and the Additional Secretary DARE are the final authority in resolving and taking decision on any situation/case of conflict, and that decision is binding on all parties concerned. For any dispute, the applicable law is Indian law under the jurisdiction of Courts in Delhi only.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your Master's is in agriculture/allied sciences with OGPA 6.60/10.0 or 65% marks or equivalent â€” this is a hard numeric gate.
Check the age gate against the last date for receipt of applications: 35 for fresh candidates, 40 for in-service candidates.
Check the freshness gate: as a fresh candidate your Master's must have been completed not more than two years before the specified date in the year of admission.
As an in-service candidate from India, confirm you are employed in the ICAR-AU system and that you can get deputation approval from your Director/Vice-Chancellor.
Choose a research topic inside the Council's identified priority areas â€” they are published one year in advance and a proposal outside them is not eligible.
Pick a host from the published lists: identified overseas institutions for Indian candidates, identified Indian Agricultural Universities in the ICAR-AU system for overseas candidates.
Apply to the host yourself and get the acceptance letter â€” ICAR makes you obtain it 'at their own level' and you must have it in hand at interview.
Write the research plan and give it a title; the form asks for discipline, degree programme, session and year of admission, prescribed duration, proposed area of study and the host's contact person.
Nominate two referees with email addresses â€” one your current supervisor (if employed) and one an expert in your area. ICAR will contact them directly.

Assemble the certified pieces early, because they take longest: the doctor's physical fitness certificate with seal, and â€” for overseas applicants â€” the Indian Diplomatic Mission certificates with office seal.
Attach copies of your academic documents, a recent photograph, supporting documents for achievements, and copies of research papers for publications above NAAS 4.0.
If you are an Indian candidate, have your Aadhar number ready â€” it is mandatory to receive the fellowships.
Email the whole pack to adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com with the subject exactly as "Application for NSIF: [your name] and [contact number]" by the deadline.
Plan your financial buffer: host fees, medical insurance and medical fitness come out of your own pocket or out of the fellowship.
important_advice_for_students: This is not full funding. ICAR states plainly that 'All fees chargeable by the host institution where the fellow is enrolled will be paid by the fellow himself out of the fellowship grant or from his/her own resources', and that all other costs including medical insurance come from the fellowship or your own resources. Model the host tuition fee before you commit.

You get the air ticket, and it is genuinely generous: a to-and-fro economy class ticket provided by the Council for both Indian and overseas candidates. But for Indian candidates, getting to the departure airport in India and from the arrival airport to the overseas university is on you or your sponsor.
For overseas fellows in India, the Council also reimburses economy-class travel from the port of arrival to your university and back â€” worth claiming.

Budget for three years and no more. The tenure 'will not be extended in any case'. If you are slow, you finish on your own money, and if you are two years past the prescribed programme duration the Council may recover the fellowship paid.

The stakes on conduct are high. Unsatisfactory performance or conduct probation terminates the fellowship immediately and makes you pay for the rest of the programme. Indian Fellows who do not return to India face recovery of the entire amount paid plus 10% overhead, and the Indian Embassy in the host country may be informed.

Do not move or change your research direction. You must sign an undertaking that you will neither change the place of work nor deviate from the broad research area, and progress is certified every six months by your advisor.

If you are an overseas fellow and your work needs Indian field trials, you may spend up to one-and-a-half-year in India and you keep the same fellowship rate during that time â€” but interim trips beyond that need your Advisor's consent and prior ICAR approval, and ICAR funds no travel for them.

Prepare for the money mechanics. The first six months are released only after ICAR receives your acceptance and your host's admission letter, and the first installment to an Indian fellow is paid in Indian Rupees only.

Indian fellows must put up an irrevocable US$ 10,000 bank guarantee in favour of the Secretary, ICAR for the whole programme. Foreign national fellows instead have Rs. 2,00,000 recovered from their grant (Rs. 1,00,000 each from the first two installments), refunded at final release. These are different mechanisms â€” know which applies to you.
The interview may not be a video call you choose. The Committee can use teleconferencing, and overseas candidates may be interviewed by Council-identified experts based in their home country.

ICAR shares in your IP. The Council takes an appropriate share on patents and knowledge generated under its IP Management bulletin, and any other IP agreement you sign must be shared with ICAR. Acknowledge ICAR support in all publications.

Note the 30-fellowship cap: allocation between Indian and overseas candidates depends on the availability of good candidates in the priority areas, so a strong topic matters as much as a strong record.
common_rejection_risks: Master's degree below OGPA 6.60/10.0 or 65% marks or equivalent.
Over the age limit on the last date prescribed for receipt of applications (35 fresh, 40 in-service).
As a fresh candidate, having completed the qualifying degree more than two years before the specified date in the year of admission.
As an in-service candidate from India, not being employed in the ICAR-AU system.
Proposed research outside the Council's identified priority areas.
No acceptance letter from the host â€” you must have one, and you must produce it at the interview.
Naming a host that is not on the identified list, or a host without the required research and teaching capability and faculty/infrastructure strength.
Only one referee, or two referees who do not meet the published composition (current supervisor plus an expert in the area).
Missing, unsealed or unsigned certificates â€” the physical fitness certificate needs a doctor's seal, and overseas applicants' certificates need the Indian Diplomatic Mission's office seal.
Missing the Certificate from the Candidate including the return-home undertaking.
Missing supporting documents: academic document copies, recent photograph, achievement documents, or copies of research papers for NAAS-above-4.0 publications.
An in-service candidate who cannot produce deputation approval, or an Indian in-service candidate who will not execute the three-year service bond.
No Aadhar number for an Indian candidate, which ICAR states is mandatory to receive the fellowships.
A wrong or missing email subject line â€” ICAR specifies "Application for NSIF: Name of Applicant and contact number".
Missing the deadline. For the 2026 cycle the last date was September 25, 2026.
estimated_uncovered_costs: All host institution fees where the fellow is enrolled â€” explicitly the fellow's own responsibility, out of the grant or own resources.
Medical insurance â€” explicitly excluded; the fellow meets it from the fellowship or own resources.
The medical fitness test â€” at the fellow's own cost.
For Indian candidates going abroad: travel from residence/work to the port of departure in India, and from the port of arrival to the destination University overseas.
Interim visits to India by overseas fellows â€” ICAR provides no financial support on travelling for the purpose.
Completion costs if the Ph.D. is not finished within the three-year tenure, or recovery of the fellowship paid if it is not finished two years beyond the prescribed programme duration.
For Indian fellows: the working capital tied up in the US$ 10,000 irrevocable bank guarantee held for the whole programme.
For foreign national fellows: Rs. 2,00,000 withheld from the grant until final release.
Books, equipment, fieldwork and consumables beyond the annual contingent and preparatory lump sum of US$ 1,000 (Indian fellows abroad) or INR 25,000 (overseas fellows in India).
document_audit: Completed application form in the prescribed ICAR proforma, signed with date and place.
Recent photograph of the applicant â€” a stated form item.
Copies of documents for every academic qualification from the graduate degree onwards, showing university/institution, degree, year, subjects and marks/grades/OGPA.
Supporting documents for professional work experience and achievements: awards/honours/scholarships (Gold Medal, Best Thesis, NTS, JRF), NET, ARS, research/teaching experience.

Publications above NAAS 4.0 only, in the prescribed four-column format (authors and title, name of journal, journal ID, NAAS score against the NAAS list of Science journals 2025), with copies of the research papers attached.
Acceptance letter for admission from the Host University â€” copy to be attached.
Copy of the research plan â€” YES/NO indicated and the copy attached.
Deputation permission from the parent organisation for in-service candidates.
Certificate from the Candidate: truth declaration, agreement to the guidelines/terms and conditions, and the undertaking to complete the Ph.D. and return to their country. Signed.

Certificate from the Indian Diplomatic Representative (overseas applicants only): permanent domicile certification, the return-to-country-of-domicile undertaking, and certification that the entries were checked against original documents and the application is complete, with scanned copies of relevant certificates enclosed. Must carry signature, name, designation, OFFICE SEAL, address, date and place.

Certificate of Physical Fitness by an authorized Medical Doctor: medical history, physical examination, lungs, summary, the doctor's view on ability to carry a full course of study involving long hours of work, health rating (EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR), vaccination record and general remarks. Must carry signature, address, date and DOCTOR's SEAL.

Certificate of Proficiency in English (overseas applicants only): whether the applicant is proficient/not proficient in written/spoken English and/or has/has not passed the English Proficiency Test, naming the conducting authority, under the SEAL of the Indian Diplomatic Mission.
Referee comment forms, one per referee, in the prescribed FORMAT: referee's name, designation, affiliation, contact phone, email; the three declarations; signature and date.
Passport details (number, date of issue, place of issue, date of expiry) and, for Indian candidates, the Aadhar number.
Fresh/in-service tick, with the Master's completion year for fresh candidates or the employer's name, address, head of organization and position held for in-service candidates.

Health advisory to action on: those planning to study in India are strongly advised to get vaccinated against typhoid/cholera before coming to India; those proceeding for overseas studies may get appropriate vaccination as per the host country's requirements.
Publication check: ICAR's document publishes no file size limit, accepted file extension or translation rule, so those remain to be confirmed with the ADG (HRD) at ICAR before you send.

referee_tracking.instructions: One of the two referees should preferably be the applicant's supervisor in the current occupation (if employed). The applicant supplies the referee's name, address, contact phone number and e-mail address; the Council may contact the referees directly to obtain comments in the prescribed format. The referee completes the 'FORMAT FOR REFEREE COMMENTS ON THE SUITABILITY OF CANDIDATE FOR NETAJI SUBHAS-ICAR INTERNATIONAL FELLOWSHIP', which asks them to state whether they are well acquainted with the applicant's work and achievements, whether they are satisfied the applicant has the sincerity, zeal and capacity to complete the Ph.D. programme applied for with funding support under the fellowship, and whether they would recommend the applicant without hesitation â€” then signs and dates it.

referee_tracking.role: Referee 2 â€” expert in the area
referee_tracking.instructions: The second referee should be an expert in the area and well acquainted with the candidate's work. The applicant supplies the name, address, contact phone number and e-mail address, and ICAR may contact this referee directly using the prescribed referee comment format, with signature and date.

Not a referee in the assessment sense, but the host's advisor/supervisor/head of institution certifies every academic progress report that the fellow submits to the Council, and those certified reports are the condition for each subsequent release of the fellowship.

A certifying authority rather than an academic referee. The mission certifies that the applicant is permanently domiciled in the named country and will return to the country of domicile on completion of studies in the host country; certifies that the entries in the application form, particulars about examinations passed, marks obtained, subjects studied and syllabi covered have been checked with original documents and that the application is complete in all respects; and confirms the applicant has enclosed scanned copies of relevant certificates, diplomas or degrees. Requires signature, name, designation, office seal, address, date and place.

Completes the Certificate of Physical Fitness, including medical history, physical examination, lungs, summary, an explicit statement on whether the applicant is or is not physically able to carry on a full course of study involving long hours of work in a college/university/institution in India or abroad, a health rating, the small pox vaccination record, and whether there is evidence of communicable disease, fatigue or physical defects. Requires signature, address, date and doctor's seal.
