application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are not an Indian citizen by birth or naturalization and do not hold an OCI/PIO card â€” otherwise this route does not apply to you.
Register on the Study in India (SII) portal. IIT Kanpur calls this mandatory and says it is also linked to issuance of your study visa, so do it before anything else.

Pick one funding route and meet its own condition: ICCR, Study in India, AARDO (AARDO member country, MTech only), India Bhutan Friendship (Bhutanese, MTech), ASEAN-DIA (currently on hold), or the Institute Fellowship (no other funding).
Match your degree to a published programme and department, and check that department's eligibility minimum â€” the published figures are absolute minimums and departments may add more.

Assemble: passport/citizenship card, applicant photo, applicant signature, proof of date of birth, qualifying degree certificate (original/provisional), GATE score card if you have one, and the mark/grade sheet of the qualifying degree as a single PDF file.
Add the NOC only if you are a sponsored, part-time or external candidate.
Apply in the right window: Autumn 20 March â€“ 15 April, or Spring 1 September â€“ 31 October for PhD only.
Submit through Pingala, or use the Foreign National email route with IIT Kanpur's offline sample form if the portal has closed.
Do not pay the application fee â€” it is waived for the Foreign National category, and you are asked to ignore the Pingala payment prompt after submitting.
Do not let a missing GATE score stop you â€” the GATE requirement is waived for the Foreign National category.
Be ready for a video-conferencing interview if shortlisted, and accept that departmental committees make the final admission decision.
important_advice_for_students: Do not read 'Institute Fellowship at par with Indian students' as full funding. Foreign students pay a published fee structure on top: USD 250 to USD 4,000 in tuition depending on programme and SAARC status, plus INR 17,495 hostel fee. Budget for that.

The single exception on tuition is the AARDO Fellowship, which waives tuition and gives free accommodation plus airfare to and from New Delhi â€” but it is for MTech only and for AARDO member countries in Asia and Africa.
The cheapest route to a scholarship may be Study in India: apply there, sit the PRAGATII exam, and meritorious students are selected for up to USD 3,200 covering tuition, accommodation and mess.
If you already hold another scholarship, you lose the Institute Fellowship â€” it is explicitly limited to students who receive no other funding. Do not count on both.
The Study in India registration is not paperwork you can defer. IIT Kanpur links it to your study visa, so a missing registration can block your visa and therefore your admission.

Two real advantages: the application fee is waived and the GATE requirement is waived for the Foreign National category. Do not let a missing GATE score stop you, and do not attempt to pay a fee you do not owe.

Watch the two-stage assistantship structure if you are a PhD candidate: Rs. 37,000/- per month for the first two years, then Rs. 42,000/- for another three years. The rate steps up, so your later years are better funded.

If you want the assistantship, you must be a regular candidate. M Tech/MS (By Research) in Cybersecurity is explicitly for sponsored/part-time/external candidates and carries no financial assistantship.

Be practical about the assistantship duty: MTech, MDes and MS (By Research) assistants are assigned 8 hours of work per week, and the institute states you are expected to carry out the assigned duties during the programme.

The email route for foreign nationals has its own, later deadline than the portal. For 2026-27 the portal closed April 15 at 02:00 PM but foreign nationals could still email until April 30, 2026 â€” do not assume the portal and email deadlines coincide.
Applications to ICCR are usually April-June, which is a different calendar from IIT Kanpur's own windows. If you are routing through ICCR, you are managing two deadlines.
ASEAN-DIA is on hold. If that was your plan, it is not available right now, and the ASEAN portal is a different route hosted at IIT Delhi.
Departments can set requirements above the published minimums, so treat the eligibility table as a floor and confirm with your target department before you invest effort.
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an Indian citizen or OCI/PIO card holder through the foreign-national route, where those candidates are not treated as foreign nationals.
Missing the mandatory Study in India registration, which is also linked to study visa issuance.
Applying outside the published windows (Autumn 20 March â€“ 15 April; Spring 1 September â€“ 31 October for PhD).
Missing the Foreign National email deadline because you assumed it matched the Pingala portal closure date.
Splitting the qualifying mark/grade sheet into multiple files when it must be a single PDF file.
Applying for the assistantship while sponsored, part-time or external â€” assistantship is limited to regular students.
Applying for M Tech/MS (By Research) in Cybersecurity as a regular candidate â€” it is sponsored/part-time/external only and carries no assistantship.
Counting on the Institute Fellowship while also holding another scholarship â€” it is limited to students with no other funding.
Relying on the ASEAN-DIA fellowship, which is published as currently on hold.
Applying for the India Bhutan Friendship Scholarship as a non-Bhutanese student, or for AARDO from a non-member country.
Being below the department's actual requirement, where the department has set a bar above the published absolute minimum.
Failing to prepare for, or attend, the video-conferencing interview that decides the final selection of shortlisted FN candidates.
Attempting to pay the waived application fee on the Pingala Portal after submission.
Not sending the required testimonials with the emailed Foreign National application.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees for every route other than the AARDO Fellowship: USD 250 (PhD SAARC), USD 500 (PhD Non-SAARC), USD 500 (MTech SAARC), USD 750 (MTech Non-SAARC), USD 2,000 (MBA SAARC) or USD 4,000 (MBA Non-SAARC).
The hostel fee of INR 17,495 in every row of the fee structure table, except under the AARDO Fellowship which includes free accommodation.
Books, equipment, travel and everyday living costs beyond the monthly fellowship or assistantship and the annual scheme-specific items.
The gap between the India Bhutan Friendship Scholarship's 'fully funded' description and any cost not named in it â€” IIT Kanpur publishes no itemised coverage for that scholarship.
Any cost attached to the Study in India route above the capped USD 3,200 scholarship.
Travel to and from India for everyone except AARDO beneficiaries, for whom airfare to and from New Delhi is published.
Medical insurance and other personal costs â€” not published as covered by any of these schemes.

official.description: The Rotary Foundation awards up to 50 fellowships a year for master's degrees and up to 120 for certificate studies at Rotary Peace Centers hosted by partner universities. Rotary states that the fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses.
purpose: Develop the capacity of peace and development professionals to become effective catalysts for peace
Support dedicated leaders from around the world through academic training, practice, and global networking opportunities
Train peace and development leaders who are committed to community and international service and the pursuit of peace
Build networks of academics, peace workers and Rotary members, and keep alumni connected to their regional peace fellow community

official.degree_award: Two tracks: a full master's degree at a Rotary Peace Center host university, or a postgraduate professional development certificate (no degree). Rotary states the fellowships may not be used for doctoral study.
official.duration: Master's programs last 15 to 24 months and include a two- to three-month field study designed by the participant. The professional development certificate program is one year of blended learning with 11 weeks of on-site participation (a two-week preliminary online course, a ten-week on-site course with field studies, a nine-month social change initiative with interactive online sessions, and a one-week on-site capstone seminar).
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle named by academic-year span (for example 2027-28, 2028-29). Applications are submitted between February and 15 May, and selected candidates are notified in November.
official.deadline_central_display: Submit your application between February and 15 May

official.description: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT), now in its 11th edition, is a scholarship programme of the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia for citizens of 23 listed countries to attend a higher education course in Italy at Master's or Postgraduate level. Winners receive an annual scholarship of EUR 10,800 paid quarterly over a 9-month period starting 1 October 2026, plus exemption from enrolment fees and university contributions, with certain named exceptions. Bachelor's or single-cycle applicants: have a non-Italian secondary school diploma ready
Master's applicants: have your foreign degree diploma ready

Pick an English-taught first-cycle/Bachelor's, single-cycle or master's degree at Padua and read that course's Admission Notice deadline, because the scholarship deadline follows the course application deadline
Confirm you are not already holding another scholarship, which disqualifies you from receiving this one
Prepare the admission documents for your degree course; there is no separate scholarship form and no extra documentation
Diary the acceptance deadline once results are published, because acceptance is by a specific notice with its own deadline
Diary 30 November of your first academic year as the 20 CFU (ECTS credits) checkpoint
important_advice_for_students: Do not look for a separate Padua International Excellence Scholarship form. Applying for the degree course of your interest automatically makes you eligible to compete for the award, and the University states there is no need to submit a separate application or any additional documentation

Weigh up the full cost before applying: the award is EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year plus a student-fee exemption, but you still pay the regional fee and the revenue stamp, and you pay full student tuition fees until graduation once the 2-year (master's) or 3-year (bachelor's/single-cycle) scholarship period ends
The award is not a full-funding package. Living costs, accommodation and travel are not mentioned anywhere in the published coverage, so budget for them yourself
Plan your ECTS credits. The scholarship is revoked if you do not earn at least 20 CFU by 30 November of the following academic year, and revoked awards must be returned
Do not transfer to another university or withdraw from your studies. Either action revokes the scholarship and obliges you to return installments already received
Accept the benefit within the deadline in the specific notice you receive; the notice sets its own acceptance procedure and deadline
Check the Call for Application when it is published in November 2026, because the detailed requirements will be set there rather than on the overview page

Note that the English version of the site is a machine-assisted translation and only the official Italian version has legal validity; rely on the Italian Call for Application for anything that will be disputed
common_rejection_risks: Missing the degree course Admission Notice deadline, since the scholarship deadline is the course application deadline and there is no separate scholarship window
Holding Italian citizenship without it being a dual citizenship
Being resident in Italy at the time of application
Missing the required qualification: a non-Italian secondary school diploma for bachelor's/single-cycle, or a foreign degree diploma for master's
Applying to a degree programme that is not completely held in English
Being a recipient of another scholarship, which bars receipt of this one
Failing to complete enrolment at the University of Padua
Earning fewer than 20 CFU (ECTS credits) by 30 November of the following academic year, which revokes the award and requires the installments to be returned
Transferring to another university or applying to withdraw from studies, which revokes the award
Missing the deadline to accept the financial benefit stated in the selection notice
Underestimating competition: the University states the selection is highly competitive and only the highest-scoring candidates with the best course track succeed
estimated_uncovered_costs: Regional tuition fee, payable every academic year - the University states beneficiaries are 'only required to pay the regional fee and the revenue stamp'
Revenue stamp (imposta di bollo), payable every academic year
Full student tuition fees for any study period after the scholarship's maximum duration, which runs until graduation
Accommodation, food and day-to-day living costs - not mentioned in the published coverage
Travel to and from Padua, and any field-study or course-specific travel costs - not mentioned in the published coverage
Books, materials and equipment - not mentioned in the published coverage
Visa and residence-permit costs - not mentioned in the published coverage
Any Italian tax on the gross scholarship amount is not addressed; the University publishes the award as gross
document_audit: Non-Italian secondary school diploma (bachelor's and single-cycle applicants) - required qualification
Foreign degree diploma (master's applicants) - required qualification
Admission documents for the chosen degree programme - the only documents required; the University states no additional documentation is needed for the scholarship
Acceptance of the financial benefit using the specific notice issued to selected candidates - note the acceptance deadline stated in that notice
No published file type, file size, translation or certification rule is given on the programme page; each degree course's own Admission Notice governs its own document format rules
The English version of the University website is machine-assisted translated and only the official Italian version has legal validity

referee_tracking.instructions: The Padua International Excellence Scholarship page publishes no referee or recommendation requirement. Any academic references required will come from the admission documents of the individual degree programme, so check the specific course's Admission Notice. If you require a declaration of academic excellence, ask the degree course's Teaching Committee through the Global Engagement Office contact form.

alerts.message: The University states the Call for Application with full detail about the Padua International Excellence Scholarships will be published in November 2026. Read it as soon as it appears.

Open the Admission Notice of each English-taught course you are considering. The scholarship deadline is the course application deadline and only the highest-scoring candidates on the best course track win.
Check you are not resident in Italy, you do not hold sole Italian citizenship, and you are not already the holder of another scholarship. Any of these removes you from the award.
Results appear on the University assessment results page. If selected, read the specific notice carefully for the acceptance procedure and its deadline.

alerts.trigger: 30 November of the first academic year
alerts.message: You must have earned at least 20 CFU (ECTS credits) by this date or the scholarship is revoked and must be returned.

official.description: The Bicocca International Scholarship Programme (BISP) is reserved for international students resident abroad, holding a foreign qualification and admitted to one of seventeen named English-taught degree programmes at the University of Milano-Bicocca. Each scholarship consists of EUR 10,000 per academic year (gross amount) and includes exemption from tuition fees; beneficiaries are not exempt from paying the administrative fee and the regional tax.
purpose: Provide financial support to talented international students and encourage access to degree programmes at the University of Milano-Bicocca
Reward academic excellence and global potential among the best students from all over the world
Support the University's growing international community, with five scholarships dedicated to each international course to ensure a wide and fair opportunity for top-tier candidates
degree_levels: Single-cycle degree (Laurea Magistrale a Ciclo Unico)
study_type: Full-time enrolment in one of the seventeen English-taught degree programmes listed in Article 1 of the call
official.degree_award: Full degree. The scholarship attaches to admission to a named Bachelor's, single-cycle or Master's degree programme and is renewable for up to 3 years for Bachelor and single-cycle degrees and 2 years for Master degrees.
official.duration: Renewable for a maximum of 3 years for Bachelor (Laurea) programmes and single-cycle degree programmes (Laurea Magistrale a Ciclo Unico), and 2 years for Master degree programmes (Laurea Magistrale).
official.application_cycle: Annual, named by academic year. The call read is the Call for Applications for the Bicocca International Scholarship Programme A.Y. 2026/27, published January 2026 and last updated 16/07/2026.
official.deadline_central_display: For free entrance (open access) courses: be admitted and have confirmed the admission offer by 15 March 2026 at the latest. Priority is given to candidates who have applied to the first Call for Admission. Each limited access course has its own admission deadlines, to be found on apply.unimib.it.
official.deadline_institutional: Limited access programmes run to their own course deadlines, published on apply.unimib.it; scholarship results for limited access programmes are published following the publication of the admission ranking list.
official.deadline_note: The only hard date published for the scholarship itself is 15 March 2026, and it applies to free access (open access) courses. Limited access courses use their own admission deadlines.
official.funding_label: Bicocca International Scholarship Programme (BISP) - EUR 10,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from tuition fees; five scholarships per eligible course, 100 in total
official.funding_period: per academic year, paid in two instalments in the first year
official.tuition_coverage: Tuition fees are exempted for the scholarship holder. Beneficiaries are not exempt from paying the administrative fee and the regional tax. A withdrawing student retains the tuition fee exemptions for the academic year of reference but must refund the amounts received.
official.tuition_rule: The scholarship includes exemption from tuition fees at the University of Milano-Bicocca for the awarded degree programme. The University pays the tuition exemption directly and requires the beneficiary to enrol for renewal years by paying only the administrative fee. Beneficiaries remain liable for the administrative fee and the regional tax.
official.host_institution_fee: Beneficiaries are not exempt from paying the administrative fee and the regional tax. For renewal years, enrolment is possible by paying only the administrative fee.
official.tax_status: Bicocca International Scholarships are considered as a form of income by the current Italian tax regulation and are subject to the tax regulations in force. The award is published as a gross amount.

Exemption from tuition fees

official.selection_notes: Scholarships are awarded by a specific Committee nominated through an Executive Decree of the Head of the Education and Student Affairs Division, whose members are the Coordinators of each degree Programme or their delegates. Five scholarships are assigned to the best candidates for each course; if additional funds become available the number allocated to each programme may be increased at the discretion of the awarding body. Results are published on apply.unimib.it by the middle of April for free access study programmes and following publication of the admission ranking list for limited access study programmes. If a beneficiary fails a requirement in Article 7.1 within the deadline set by the office, the scholarship is awarded to the next eligible student in the ranking list.

important_advice_for_students: Do not look for a BISP application form. The University states applicants are not required to send or fill out any application form other than applying to the relevant Bachelor's or Master's programme

Watch your e-mail account registered on the Dream Apply platform. All communication about scholarship awarding and deadlines is sent exclusively through that platform, so a filtered or unmonitored e-mail account is a real risk of losing the award

Do not confuse the scholarship with a fee waiver. You get EUR 10,000 gross per year plus tuition exemption, but you still pay the administrative fee and the regional tax, and the call says nothing about accommodation, food or travel
Budget for the tax. The call states the scholarship is considered income under current Italian tax regulation and is subject to the tax regulations in force, and the amount is published as gross
Bank your first exam. The second instalment depends on passing at least one exam in the first semester, and credits recognised from previous studies are not counted towards it

Do not accept DSU benefits in parallel. The scholarship cannot be combined with the DSU regional scholarship or with DSU-connected benefits such as the meal card, housing or extraordinary grant; if you are offered an incompatible award you must choose within ten days of the most recent awarding
Note the one good piece of news: the scholarship is compatible with international mobility grants

If you need to pause your studies, apply for suspension of the scholarship by emailing international.promotion@unimib.it and justify it. Suspension cannot last more than one academic year, and simply stopping without applying risks full withdrawal

Read the ranking PDFs the University publishes. The call states that for limited access courses scholarships follow the published admission ranking list, so your admission position is effectively your scholarship position
If you are admitted to a course whose admission is managed by a partner University, expect the scholarship to follow the ranking shared by that partner University, not a separate selection

Italian or SEPA bank account in the beneficiary student's own name - required before the first instalment is paid

referee_tracking.instructions: The BISP call publishes no referee, recommendation or reference-letter requirement. Selection for limited access courses is purely by published admission ranking list, and for free access courses by an Evaluation Committee scoring academic excellence and past education records. Any references required come from the individual degree programme's own admission procedure, so check apply.unimib.it for your specific course. Do not spend effort on referees for BISP itself.

alerts.message: Check your course appears in the seventeen programmes listed in Article 1 of the call. Outside that list there is no BISP.
Confirm you are not resident in Italy, are not a non-EU resident with a permit to stay, are not an EU resident of over nine months, have never studied a master's in Italy, and hold no other grant.
Published cut-off for free access (open access) courses to confirm the admission offer. Limited access courses have their own deadlines on apply.unimib.it.
Scholarship selection results for free access programmes are published on apply.unimib.it. Check the ranking PDFs the University publishes.
Accept the scholarship offer officially by the stated deadline and send everything to the e-mail account registered on the Dream Apply platform.
First instalment conditions must be met: completed enrolment and documents within deadlines, an Italian or SEPA account in your own name, and a signed Declaration of Acceptance form.
You must have arrived in Milan. Non-EU students need the Italian student visa (D - enrolment).
Second instalment is paid only after verification that you passed at least one exam in the first semester.
Renewal checkpoints: 40 ECTS then 60 ECTS. Miss them and the scholarship is fully withdrawn and refunded.
BISP cannot be combined with DSU or any other Italian or foreign grant, nor with DSU meal card, housing or extraordinary grant. You must choose within ten days of the most recent awarding.

submission_workflow: Select one of the seventeen eligible English-taught degree programmes
Check whether it is limited access or free access, and find the applicable deadlines on apply.unimib.it
Apply to the programme on the Dream Apply platform and use an e-mail account you will actually read
Pay the admission deposit so your offer counts as accepted
Limited access: complete all admission procedures and confirm the offer by the course deadline. Free access: confirm the admission offer by 15 March 2026
Check the published admission ranking and the University ranking PDFs
Wait for the scholarship results on apply.unimib.it
If selected, read the offer from the International Global Engagement Unit on the platform and accept it officially by its deadline
Confirm you hold no other scholarship or DSU-connected benefit
Open an Italian or SEPA bank account in your own name and sign the Declaration of Acceptance form
Start the Italian student visa (D - enrolment) if you are a non-EU student
Complete enrolment with all required documents, passing document authenticity and enrolment eligibility checks
Arrive in Milan by 31 October 2026
Pass at least one exam in the first semester to receive the second instalment
Track credits towards 40, 60, 90 and 120 ECTS to keep renewing the award
post_award_requirements: Arrive in Milan by 31 October 2026
Complete enrolment following checks on document authenticity and enrolment eligibility
Open and maintain an Italian or SEPA bank account in your own name for payment
Pass at least one exam in the first semester; credits recognised from previous studies are not counted
Meet the renewal credit requirements: 40 ECTS by November 2027, 60 ECTS by March 2028, 90 ECTS by November 2028 and 120 ECTS by March 2029
Do not hold any other grant or DSU-connected benefit, and exercise the right of choice within ten days if an incompatible award is assigned
Request and justify any suspension of the scholarship by emailing international.promotion@unimib.it; suspension cannot exceed one academic year
Pay the administrative fee and the regional tax, and the administrative fee again for each renewal year
Refund amounts already received if the scholarship is withdrawn, while retaining the tuition fee exemptions for the academic year of reference
Accept that the University verifies the accuracy of statements even after award, and that untruthful statements constitute a crime under Italian law
Treat the award as taxable income under current Italian tax regulation
questions_to_ask_host: Is my degree programme one of the seventeen listed in Article 1, and is it limited access or free access?
What is my exact admission deadline, and when is the deposit due so my offer counts as accepted?
Where do I appear on the official admission ranking list, and how does that ranking translate into the scholarship ranking?
What is the administrative fee and the regional tax I will have to pay on top of the tuition exemption?
What do the EUR 10,000 gross actually have to cover, and what do students typically spend it on?
When is the Declaration of Acceptance form sent, and what is the acceptance deadline in the offer?
What are the enrolment document requirements and the deadline for submitting them?
If I am a non-EU student, what are the current Italian student visa (D - enrolment) requirements and processing times?
How is my course's credit requirement structured, and how are credits recognised from my previous study counted given that they are not counted for the second instalment?
If my course's admission is managed by a partner University, how is the partner ranking applied to the BISP selection?
Are there any Bicocca accommodation or canteen options available to a BISP holder, given the DSU meal card and housing benefits are incompatible with this scholarship?

official.application_cycle: Academic year 2027-2028, with session-specific application windows
official.deadline_central_display: First year BSc and law programmes, Early session and HEC 1st round for international candidates: November 12 - 30 November 2026
official.deadline_note: The award runs multiple session-specific windows and only one application may be submitted per session. For first year BSc and law: international candidates in the Early session and HEC 1st round, 12 to 30 November 2026; solo italiani in the same sessions, 11 to 22 January 2027; winter session and HEC 2nd round, 15 March to 5 April 2027; spring session for Italian candidates, 27 May to 4 June 2027. For first year MSc: international applicants 28 January to 8 February 2027, 4 to 18 March 2027, 13 to 27 April 2027, and 10 to 18 June 2027; Bocconi and Italian applicants 28 January to 8 February 2027, 27 May to 7 June 2027, and 8 to 15 June 2027. For PhD students and students in years after the first, 25 May to 25 June 2027. 30 November 2026 is recorded as the earliest deadline. The 2026-2027 page carries a warning that the assistance and services assigned for one academic year are not automatically granted for later years, so the application must be submitted every year of enrolment.
official.status_note: The 2027-2028 deadlines page was published with 'page being updated' and links opening as the application period approaches, but the listed dates start 12 November 2026, which is after today's date of 1 October 2026, so the earliest window is upcoming. Bocconi states the deadlines are final.
official.funding_period: per academic year
official.funding_duration: Tied to enrolment, renewable each academic year by reapplication
official.tuition_coverage_note: The published benefits for a.y. 2026-2027 are a free daily meal, valued at the LOMBARDY REGION rate of 829 euros, a second free daily meal from the canteen, preferential rates in the Bocconi restaurant and cafe, a 200-hour work-study opportunity with 14 euros per hour, and a cash contribution in a second instalment of 3,000 euros for high-merit applicants. The page does not state a tuition fee waiver, so tuition coverage is unconfirmed.
official.living_cost_coverage_note: The published benefit that can be read as living-cost support is a free daily meal in the canteen, plus preferential rates in the restaurant and cafe, and a possible cash contribution of 3,000 euros for high-merit applicants. Bocconi does not label these as living cost coverage, so this is an interpretation of published benefits rather than a stated category.
official.funding_label: ISU Bocconi Scholarship benefits, published for a.y. 2026-2027: free daily meal at 829 euros, second daily meal, preferential restaurant and cafe rates, 200-hour work-study at 14 euros per hour, and a 3,000 euro cash contribution for high-merit applicants
benefits: Free daily meal, with the value set at the rate established by the LOMBARDY REGION, which was 829 euros for a.y. 2026-2027
A second free daily meal from the canteen
Preferential rates in the Bocconi restaurant and cafe
A 200-hour work-study opportunity valued at 14 euros per hour
A second cash instalment of 3,000 euros for high-merit applicants
For international candidates, the tuition benefits described are the tuition reductions for international students
eligibility: For first year students, must be a first-time enrolled student in a Bocconi undergraduate, master of science or law programme, and students already enrolled in a year subsequent to the first are explicitly not eligible for that session

Must be enrolled in one of the Bocconi undergraduate degree courses, the master of science or the Legal Markets programme, or the IM Global, Global Law or Finance Global Experience double degree programmes
PhD students are eligible under their own application window
Must meet both economic and merit requirements

Economic requirement: an indicator of economic situation, based on ISEE or ISPE for Italian students and ISEEU or ISPEEU Parificato for international students, of no more than 26,887.93 euros for a.y. 2026-2027 for ISEE and ISEEU Parificato, and no more than 58,452.06 euros for ISPE and ISPEEU Parificato
Bocconi states the 2027-2028 values will be published in the coming months and are expected to be resolved by the Lombardy Region in June or July 2027

The scholarship is not combined with the reduced contribution for students from low-income households, called the ISU reduction, and a year of merit is not combined with the ISU reduction
official.citizenship_residency: Applies to both Italian and international students, and international candidates are treated in their own session windows. Economic assessment uses the Italian national income statement for residents or the equivalent income indicator for non-residents. The tuition benefits described for international students are set out on a separate international students page, and the international tuition reductions are distinct from the ISU Scholarship.

After submitting, periodically verify the Notifications area of MyApplication, where all communication from the Fees, Funding and Housing office is sent.
requirements: Access the online application through the link that becomes available on the deadlines page during the application period, and ignore dates shown inside the online procedure since those are standard system dates

Upload the required documents proving non-resident status for non-resident applicants
Only one application per session may be submitted

CAF confirmation email, for international candidates in the Early session

award_holder_conditions: The assistance and services assigned for one academic year are not automatically granted for later years, so it is the student's responsibility to apply every academic year of enrolment

Scholarship recipients must be enrolled full-time and are subject to the University's disciplinary rules, failing which the scholarship can be revoked

For a.y. 2026-2027 the published benefits are a free daily meal valued at 829 euros, a second free daily meal, preferential restaurant and cafe rates, a 200-hour work-study opportunity at 14 euros per hour and a 3,000 euro cash contribution for high-merit applicants. Applications run in session-specific windows for a.y. 2027-2028, from 12 November 2026 for first year BSc and law international candidates through 25 June 2027 for PhD and later-year students, and must be submitted every year of enrolment.

official.description: Sapienza University of Rome announces a call for applications for admission to 94 PhD Programmes of the 42nd cycle, based on qualifications and examinations, or examinations only. A PhD programme is the third cycle of studies and the highest level of university education in the Italian system, lasts three years, and entry is granted through a competitive selection process. Sapienza PhD scholarships are entirely financed by Sapienza at a published annual gross amount of EUR 16,243.00, plus a research budget equal to 10% of the scholarship.
purpose: Enable candidates to develop the skills required to carry out highly qualified research activities
Train researchers through the third cycle of studies, the highest level of university education within the Italian academic system
Allocate Sapienza PhD scholarships to the individual courses following resolution No. 108/2026 of the Academic Senate dated 15/05/2026
Attract and support doctoral candidates including through joint and inter-university PhD programmes agreed with funding bodies and companies
study_type: Research doctoral study based on qualifications and examinations, or examinations only
Full-time doctoral research, with a self-designed or supervisor-guided project developed within a doctoral school
official.degree_award: Full PhD degree (Doctor of Philosophy), third cycle. Admission requires a second-cycle degree. Some programmes are joint degrees, for example Astronomy with the University of Rome Tor Vergata, where a joint degree is awarded on completion of the cycle.
official.duration: The duration of a PhD programme is three years. The duration of the scholarship is equal to the legal duration of the programme.
official.application_cycle: Annual, named by academic year and cycle number (Academic Year 2026/2027 - 42nd Cycle, issued by Rectoral Decree No. 998/2026 of 15/05/2026, Prot. n. 68062/2026). A separate pre-selection call exists for citizens of the People's Republic of China under the Sapienza-CSC agreement.
official.deadline_central_display: Applications must be submitted by 17 June 2026 at 14:00 (local time - CET) without any exception. The application fee must be paid through the PagoPA system no later than 17 June 2026 at 14:00 (local time - CET).
official.deadline_institutional: Each individual PhD programme publishes its own admission procedures and evaluation criteria on its programme web page under the 'Call for application (42nd cycle)' section, and holds its examination dates separately. Candidates who anticipate completing their master's degree by 31 October 2026 must also have obtained the required degree by that date, or are admitted with reserve.
official.deadline_note: A separate published deadline exists for the China Scholarship Council pre-selection: 24 February 2026 at 14:00 (local time - CET) for Chinese candidates applying under the Sapienza-CSC agreement for the 42nd cycle.
official.funding_label: Sapienza PhD scholarship (scholarships entirely financed by Sapienza, plus scholarships financed by Departments, Departments of Excellence, public or private bodies, other Universities, or the Italian Science Fund FIS)
official.funding_period: per year gross of statutory withholdings, paid on a monthly basis, for the legal duration of the programme
official.living_cost_coverage: No tuition applies to a PhD programme as such, but all admitted candidates must pay a stamp duty of EUR 16.00 and a regional tax of EUR 140.00 on enrolment.
official.travel_coverage: The scholarship amount is increased up to 50% for authorised periods abroad up to 12 months (extendable to a total of 18 months for joint PhDs with international institutions). Every PhD student, with or without scholarship, has a budget for research activities in Italy and abroad corresponding to 10% of the amount of the scholarship.
official.tuition_rule: PhD programmes at Sapienza do not carry tuition fees. All admitted candidates must instead pay a stamp duty of EUR 16.00 and a regional tax of EUR 140.00 on enrolment. Admitted candidates with a recognised disability of at least 66% or a disability recognised under Article 3, paragraph 3 or paragraph 1 of Law No. 104 of 05/02/1992 are exempt from paying the regional tax and must evidence their status by emailing ufficio.dottorato@uniroma1.it.
official.host_institution_fee: Stamp duty of EUR 16.00 plus regional tax of EUR 140.00 payable by all admitted candidates on enrolment, with a regional tax exemption for recognised disabled candidates.
official.tax_status: The annual amount of the scholarship is EUR 16,243.00 gross of statutory withholdings to be paid by students, pursuant to Ministerial Decree No. 247/2022. For international students, payment of the scholarship may in any case be made only after obtaining a tax identification number (codice fiscale) issued by the competent authority or institution. The EUR 19,800.00 top-up is described as gross of welfare charges borne by the recipient.
covered_expenses: Annual PhD scholarship of EUR 16,243.00 gross paid monthly for the legal duration of the programme
Research activity budget in Italy and abroad equal to 10% of the scholarship amount, for every PhD student with or without scholarship
Scholarship increase of up to 50% for authorised periods abroad up to 12 months, extendable to 18 months for joint PhDs with international institutions
Top-up to EUR 19,800.00 for the first potential winner in the final rankings who holds a degree obtained abroad and resides abroad (maximum one per PhD programme)
Equivalent 50% allowance for PhD students without a scholarship for authorised periods of study or research abroad, maximum 12 months
not_covered_or_excluded: Stamp duty of EUR 16.00 payable by all admitted candidates
Regional tax of EUR 140.00 payable by all admitted candidates, unless exempt for recognised disability
The non-refundable participation/application fee for admission, payable through PagoPA (the amount is not stated in the call text read)

PhD scholarships cannot be combined with research fellowships or other scholarships awarded for any reason, except grants from national or foreign institutions intended to integrate the training or research activities of scholarship holders through stays abroad, and funding from the Fondo Giovani MUR
Positions without scholarship, for which it is not possible to compete directly; non-funded positions are allocated only after completion of the acceptance process for funded positions
Scholarship for any PhD programme that is not accredited under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021 will not be activated for the 42nd cycle
Third-party funded scholarships are conditional on confirmation of the funding commitment through a specific agreement, and payment is conditional on the funder disbursing the money to Sapienza
benefits: Monthly payment of a EUR 16,243.00 gross annual scholarship for the legal duration of the programme
Research activity budget in Italy and abroad equal to 10% of the scholarship amount
Scholarship increase of up to 50% for authorised periods abroad, up to 12 months or 18 months for joint PhDs with international institutions
Possible top-up to EUR 19,800.00 for the first-ranked candidate holding a foreign degree and residing abroad
Regional tax exemption on enrolment for candidates with a recognised disability
eligibility: Access to the PhD programme is open to individuals of any age and nationality

By 31 October 2026, hold a degree from the pre-Ministerial Decree 509/99 system (so-called 'old system'), or laurea specialistica and/or magistrale (Ministerial Decree No. 509/99, Ministerial Decree No. 270/2004)
Hold a second-level academic qualification issued by institutions belonging to the AFAM sector (Higher Education for Art, Music and Dance)

Hold an official foreign degree corresponding to the second cycle according to the Bologna Process qualifications framework and level 7 according to the European Qualifications Framework, which allows access to the PhD programme at academic institutions in the country where it was issued and is recognized as suitable for access to the PhD programme in Italy (Master's degree or equivalent title, in any case with a written final thesis), with no 'substantial difference' according to the Lisbon Convention principles and the CIMEA national methodology
Pay the application fee through the PagoPA system integrated into the online application form by the deadline
Declare the scholarship(s) they intend to compete for, indicating potential preferences in order of priority
Self-declare possession of the admission requirements pursuant to Article 76 of Presidential Decree No. 445/2000
general_eligibility: Open to individuals of any age and nationality
Requires a second-cycle degree (Master's, specialist, single-cycle degree, or an equivalent foreign qualification), with a written final thesis in the case of a foreign qualification
Candidates who obtain the required degree between the date of submission of the application and 31 October 2026 are admitted 'with reserve' until they obtain it
ineligibility_conditions: Those who have already benefited, even partially, from a scholarship awarded for attending a PhD or equivalent programme at this University or another university in Italy cannot benefit from another PhD scholarship; on admission they must forgo the awarded scholarship if positions without scholarship are available
Those who have already benefited from a PhD scholarship, even partially, cannot receive a second one for the same qualification
Simultaneous enrolment in more than one PhD programme, or in both a PhD programme and a first- or second-level Master's programme, for the same academic year is not allowed
Enrolment and registration for the second year of a PhD programme is incompatible with entering into a research contract pursuant to Article 22 of Law No. 240 of 30/12/2010

The annual gross personal taxable income limit to be eligible for the PhD scholarship is set at EUR 16,243.00, excluding the scholarship itself; on reaching the limit the PhD student must reimburse all scholarship instalments unduly received in the relevant tax year (1 January - 31 December of each year)

PhD scholarships cannot be combined with research fellowships or other scholarships awarded for any reason, except grants from national or foreign institutions for stays abroad and Fondo Giovani MUR funding; in case of subsequent incompatibility any unduly received instalment must be reimbursed

It is not possible to compete for non-scholarship positions; a candidate may renounce a scholarship only within the limit of the number of non-scholarship positions announced in the call, according to ranking order

Falsity in the self-certifications leads to exclusion from the competitive tests, or forfeiture if already enrolled as a winner, without prejudice to criminal sanctions under Article 76 of Presidential Decree No. 445/2000
For PhD programmes not accredited under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021, activation for the 42nd cycle will not proceed
In written examinations, use of a different ink pen, use of pencil unless required, signature, or correction fluids are reasons for exclusion
official.citizenship_residency: Open to individuals of any age and nationality. Non-EU citizens requiring an entry visa for long-term stays in Italy must hold a visa for 'post-graduate studies' and provide the Receipt of First Residence Permit Request for study purposes.
official.international_eligibility: Foreign qualifications are admitted where they correspond to the second cycle in the Bologna Process framework and level 7 EQF, allow PhD access in the country of issue, are recognised as suitable for access in Italy, and present no 'substantial difference' under the Lisbon Convention and CIMEA methodology. Applicants holding a degree obtained abroad and residing abroad who are the first potential winner in the final rankings (maximum one per PhD programme) receive an increased scholarship of EUR 19,800.00. masters: Admission requires a second-cycle degree (laurea specialistica/magistrale, or equivalent foreign second-cycle/level 7 EQF qualification with a written final thesis)

phd: The PhD is the third cycle of studies and lasts three years
Admission is by competitive selection based on qualifications and examinations, or examinations only

Winners of positions without scholarship already enrolled in previous years may reapply for the same PhD programme but must formally withdraw from their previous enrolment and notify the PhD Office - Programmes and Careers before completing the new enrolment

Those who already obtained a PhD degree without a scholarship may apply provided the predominant research topics and scientific-disciplinary sectors of the aspired PhD programme differ from those of the PhD programme for which the title was obtained

host_requirements: The PhD programme must be one of the 94 programmes listed in Annex A, which is an integral part of the call, and belong to the Doctoral School indicated there where established
Enrolment must be completed by the deadline specified in the notification sent after publication of the final rankings, or the candidate is considered to have withdrawn

Foreign degree holders must additionally provide, for enrolment, the certificate of the academic qualification, the transcript of records, and a CIMEA statement of comparability or a Declaration of Value or a Diploma Supplement, all translated into Italian or English and authenticated with an Apostille or legalized by the Italian Diplomatic Representation

All candidates must provide a passport or, for EU citizens, a valid Identity Card, a tax identification number (codice fiscale), and, where applicable, a visa for 'post-graduate studies' and residence permit documents

Candidates requiring a visa for postgraduate studies must access the UNIVERSITALY portal and complete the 'pre-enrolment application', which must be validated by the University PhD Offices and then submitted to the diplomatic or consular representation in their country of residence
PhD programmes subject to accreditation under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021 only; unaccredited programmes are not activated for the 42nd cycle
requirements: Submit the application online through INFOSTUD: log in, click on the 'PhD Programmes' section, select 'Submit a new application', fill out the online form in all its parts, upload the required documents, close and submit

documents: For candidates with a qualification obtained in a country of the European Union: a self-certification of the academic qualification with list of exams and related grades in Italian or English, pursuant to Article 3 of the call

For candidates with a qualification obtained in a NON-EU country: certification of the academic qualification with a list of exams and relative grades translated into Italian or English, authenticated through Apostille or, if the country is not a member of the Hague Convention, legalized by the Italian Diplomatic Representation (Embassy or Consulate) in the country to whose education systems the qualification refers
Valid ID for sitting the examinations
For enrolment of foreign degree holders: certificate of the academic qualification translated into Italian or English with Apostille or legalisation
For enrolment of foreign degree holders: transcript of records (ToR) translated into Italian or English with Apostille or legalisation

For enrolment of foreign degree holders: statement of comparability issued by the Italian ENIC-NARIC centre (CIMEA), or a Declaration of Value issued by the Italian Diplomatic Representation, or a Diploma Supplement issued by the competent institution and legalized or apostilled
Passport or, for EU citizens, a valid Identity Card
Visa for 'post-graduate studies' issued by the Embassy or Consulate (only for non-EU citizens requiring an entry visa for long-term stays in Italy)
Tax identification number (codice fiscale) issued by the competent authority or institution
Receipt of First Residence Permit Request for study purposes (only for citizens of non-EU countries holding a visa for 'post-graduate studies')
Valid Residence Permit (only for non-EU citizens regularly living in Italy); if expired, the Receipt of Renewal Request

document_format_rules: Qualification documentation must be in Italian or English

Disability and SLD support requests must be submitted strictly by the deadline of the call and must specify the type of support required
In written examinations candidates must only use a black ink biro pen; the paper provided must not be signed or made recognisable in any way, under penalty of exclusion
The application must be submitted through the INFOSTUD online form by uploading the required documents; once submitted it can no longer be modified or resubmitted
No file type, file size or page limit is published in the call
selection_criteria: The purpose of the admission test is to guarantee an adequate comparative evaluation of the candidates
All testing modalities and the grids containing the evaluation criteria are published on the web page of each individual PhD programme under the 'Call for application (42nd cycle)' section
A foreign language test may be required, as reported on the individual PhD Programme web pages
Tie-break for a position covered by scholarship: the candidate with the less favourable economic condition prevails, pursuant to Prime Ministerial Decree No. 159, Article 8, paragraph 4 of 05/12/2013

Tie-break for a position without scholarship, in order: higher graduation mark for the title giving access to the PhD; then higher average mark; then achievement of the degree in the shortest possible time considering the legal duration of the programme; then the younger candidate prevails

For PhD programmes with multiple curricula there is a single competition and a single Selection Committee; the examinations are the same for all curricula, though a separate set of written questions may be set for each curriculum
official.selection_notes: Selection Committees are appointed pursuant to the Sapienza PhD Regulations; for third-party or Department-funded scholarships the Selection Committees may be supplemented by a scientific expert from the funded projects. Candidates must attend examinations at the stated date, time and venue without waiting for further convocation and provide valid ID. Oral tests may be held via videoconference if specified on the programme web page, or may be requested on documented valid grounds at the absolute discretion of the Selection Committee. Results for each completed examination are published on the individual PhD programme web page, identifying candidates by matricola, and are also made available on the candidate's personal application page. Final rankings are published exclusively on https://www.uniroma1.it/it/pagina/elenco-dei-corsi-di-dottorato, indicating total score, any curriculum selected or assigned, and scholarships awarded, and candidates are admitted in descending order of merit until all announced positions are filled. Successful candidates are notified by email to the address given in the application; failure to complete enrolment within the specified timeframe is treated as withdrawal and the position passes to the next candidate. Any renunciation of the PhD programme or of the scholarship is irrevocable, and no further offers are made in the event of subsequent reassignments.

important_advice_for_students: Start early and finish early. The call states that complaints about system malfunctions near the deadline are not accepted and that the participation fee is non-refundable under any circumstances, so there is no upside to submitting in the last hour

Read your own programme's web page, not just the general call. The testing modality, the evaluation-criteria grids, the examination dates, whether a foreign language test is required and whether oral tests can be by videoconference are all published per programme, and Annex A links to each one
Do not sign the examination paper. Signing it, using anything other than a black ink biro, or using correction fluids is a stated ground for exclusion
Do not apply to a programme you cannot finish financially. You pay a EUR 16.00 stamp duty and a EUR 140.00 regional tax on enrolment, and the scholarship is the only recurring income published

Track your income carefully. The eligibility limit is EUR 16,243.00 gross personal taxable income excluding the scholarship itself, and exceeding it means repaying all instalments received in that tax year

Do not accept a second PhD scholarship. Holding one already, even partially, for the same qualification, disqualifies you, and if you are admitted you must forgo the awarded scholarship if non-scholarship positions are available
You cannot compete directly for a non-scholarship position. Non-funded positions are allocated only after all funded positions are accepted, in ranking order

If you are ranked but not funded, do not assume you are out. The rankings also record eligibility assessments for specific scholarships, and a funded awardee who renounces or fails to enrol causes reassignment in ranking order to the first eligible candidate
Renunciation is irreversible. The call states that no further offers of positions or scholarships are made in the event of subsequent reassignments

If you are already enrolled in a previous year on a non-scholarship position and win again, you must formally withdraw from the previous enrolment and notify the PhD Office - Programmes and Careers before completing the new enrolment
Check that your programme is accredited under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021; activation for the 42nd cycle does not proceed for unaccredited programmes
For Chinese applicants there is a separate, earlier route: the Sapienza-CSC pre-selection call, with its own 24 February 2026 deadline and a restricted list of programmes in the Appendix

Budget the abroad uplift correctly. Authorised periods abroad raise the scholarship by up to 50% for up to 12 months, extendable to 18 months for joint PhDs with international institutions, and non-scholarship students get an equivalent 50% allowance

Beware the incompatibility. The scholarship cannot be combined with research fellowships or other scholarships, except stays-abroad integration grants and Fondo Giovani MUR funding, and later incompatibility means repaying what you received
common_rejection_risks: A non-EU qualification that is not translated into Italian or English, or not authenticated with an Apostille or legalized by the Italian Diplomatic Representation
A foreign qualification presenting a 'substantial difference' under the Lisbon Convention and CIMEA methodology, or one that does not allow PhD access in the country where it was issued
No written final thesis in the case of a foreign qualification
Not holding the required second-cycle degree by 31 October 2026
Failing to close and submit the application in INFOSTUD, or failing to pay the application fee through PagoPA by 17 June 2026 at 14:00 CET
Paying outside the integrated PagoPA system, for example an unsolicited PagoPA payment, which the call states will not be accepted
Falsity in the self-certification, which leads to exclusion or forfeiture plus criminal sanctions under Article 76 of Presidential Decree No. 445/2000
Signing or marking the written examination paper, using a pen other than black ink, using pencil when not required, or using correction fluids
Not attending at the stated date, time and venue without waiting for further convocation, or arriving without valid ID
Exceeding the EUR 16,243.00 gross personal taxable income limit, which requires repayment of that year's instalments
Having already held, even partially, a PhD scholarship for the same qualification
Enrolling in more than one PhD programme, or in a PhD plus a first- or second-level Master's programme, in the same academic year
Entering a research contract under Article 22 of Law 240/2010 while registering for the second PhD year
Applying to a PhD programme that is not accredited under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021
Missing the enrolment deadline in the notification, which is treated as withdrawal
Missing the disability or SLD support request deadline, or submitting certification that does not name nosological codes and the specific type of SLD
Missing the 5-day documentation deadline for industrial PhD reserved positions or for supernumerary foreign state scholarship positions
estimated_uncovered_costs: Stamp duty of EUR 16.00 payable by every admitted candidate on enrolment
Regional tax of EUR 140.00 payable by every admitted candidate on enrolment, unless exempt for a recognised disability
The non-refundable participation/application fee for admission, payable through PagoPA; the call requires it but does not state the amount in the text read
Living costs in Rome, which the scholarship amount is not itemised against and the research budget of 10% is for research activities rather than subsistence
Books, equipment, conference travel and consumables beyond the 10% research activity budget in Italy and abroad
Costs of obtaining the Apostille or legalisation of qualification documents, and of sworn translations
UNIVERSITALY pre-enrolment and visa application and issuance costs for non-EU citizens requiring a visa for 'post-graduate studies'
First residence permit costs for non-EU citizens
Any fees or income loss arising from a suspension of the PhD programme, during which the scholarship is suspended for up to six months

Additional conditions apply to candidates applying for a Master in Finance, Psychology, Arts or Nursing.
official.application_method: Four stages. (1) Prepare a single PDF application file in the prescribed document order. (2) Register online and upload the PDF; the deadline for online registration is 1 November. (3) Have two letters of recommendation emailed by their authors, from a professional (not private) email address, to mastergrants@unil.ch, by 1 November - only letters sent after online registration are considered. (4) If your diploma comes from a state that has not ratified the Lisbon Convention, have your university certify and seal diplomas, transcripts and provisional certificates in an envelope with a covering letter giving the certifier's full details, and post it to UNIL SASME, Batiment Unicentre, CH-1015 Lausanne, with a 1 November postmark. The scholarship application also serves as your application for the chosen Master's degree, so a separate application to the Admissions Office is not needed.
requirements: Pay the administrative fee of CHF 200 (non-refundable, no waiver possible) with the reason 'Master's Scholarship - your first and last name' to IBAN CH17 0900 0000 1001 3575 3, SWIFT/BIC POFICHBEXXX
Hold a degree equivalent to a Swiss bachelor's (180 ECTS) from a foreign university

official.english_requirement: C1 minimum in the language of instruction of the chosen Master's (English for English-taught programmes). No language certificate is required if the chosen master's is taught in the candidate's mother tongue or the bachelor's was entirely taught in the language of the chosen master's. Candidates must check the programme page for the level required.

official.description: UNIL awards around ten Master's excellence scholarships each year, exclusively to students who graduated from a foreign university with very high academic results. The award is CHF 1,600 per month for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme, plus exemption from standard course registration fees (only the CHF 80 semester fee remains), and UNIL guarantees accommodation with the FMEL. UNIL states explicitly that the scholarship does not constitute full funding, since roughly CHF 2,000 per month is needed to live in Lausanne. The application deadline for 2027/2028 is 1 November 2026, and the scholarship application doubles as the Master's admission application.
official.program_type: University excellence scholarship for international master's students
official.coverage: Covers a CHF 1,600 monthly living stipend and standard course registration fees, plus guaranteed FMEL housing at a rent the student pays - but not UNIL tuition fees beyond the CHF 80 semester fee, and not the roughly CHF 400 per month gap between the stipend and the stated cost of living in Lausanne.

official.description: Excellence scholarships are awarded by the University of St.Gallen to students enrolled in a Bachelor's degree at the University of St.Gallen on the basis of merit. The scholarship amount corresponds to the current tuition fees at the Bachelor level for a total of 6 semesters. The University of St.Gallen and the Monique Dornonville de la Cour-Stiftung currently award these scholarships in cooperation with the Advice Center for Study Funding.
purpose: Reward outstanding academic performance among enrolled Bachelor's students at the University of St.Gallen
Recognise excellence demonstrated in the HSG Assessment Year by supporting the recipient's tuition fees for the whole Bachelor's duration
study_type: Enrolled Bachelor's degree study at the University of St.Gallen
official.degree_award: Not applicable. The scholarship is a tuition-fee award attached to an already-enrolled Bachelor's degree, not a degree or a short-term award in itself.
official.duration: The scholarship amount corresponds to the current tuition fees at the Bachelor level for a total of 6 semesters.
official.application_cycle: Invitation-based, tied to performance in the HSG Assessment Year. The Advice Center for Study Funding identifies qualifying enrolled students and invites them to apply. Published Compass submission deadlines for study funding requests are 1 October (autumn semester) and 1 March (spring semester).
official.deadline_central_display: Applications can only be made following an invitation from the University of St.Gallen; an application without an invitation is not possible. The published Compass deadlines for study funding requests are 1 October (autumn semester) and 1 March (spring semester).
official.deadline_institutional: 1 October (autumn semester) and 1 March (spring semester), the deadlines the University publishes for submitting study funding application forms including the required enclosures via Compass.
official.deadline_note: The Excellence Scholarships section of the University page does not itself state an application deadline. The 1 October and 1 March deadlines published on the same page govern submission of study funding application forms including required enclosures, and are recorded as institutional deadlines only.
official.funding_label: HSG Excellence Scholarship (Bachelor level) - awarded by the University of St.Gallen and the Monique Dornonville de la Cour-Stiftung, value equal to the current Bachelor tuition fees for 6 semesters
official.funding_period: Total of 6 semesters, equal to the current tuition fees at the Bachelor level; no per-semester or annual figure is published
official.tuition_coverage: The scholarship amount corresponds to the current tuition fees at the Bachelor level for a total of 6 semesters, so the award is expressed as full Bachelor tuition fees rather than as a cash stipend.
official.tuition_rule: The award is not a separate fee waiver negotiated with the University; it is defined by HSG as an amount corresponding to the current Bachelor tuition fees for a total of 6 semesters. No published condition attaches the waiver to continued enrolment beyond the 6-semester value, and no figure is published for the 'current tuition fees at the Bachelor level' on which the amount depends.
covered_expenses: An amount corresponding to the current tuition fees at the Bachelor level for a total of 6 semesters

In addition to the performance criterion, further selection criteria may be applied depending on the funding source. The final selection of scholarship awardees is the responsibility of the relevant committees. application_readiness_checklist: Accept that you cannot apply on your own initiative. HSG states an application without an invitation from the University is not possible

important_advice_for_students: Do not treat this as a scholarship you can apply for. The invitation is the entry requirement, and HSG states plainly that an application without an invitation is not possible. Direct the effort into the Assessment Year instead

Understand what you are actually getting. The award equals the current Bachelor tuition fees for 6 semesters, so it is a tuition award, not a living-cost grant. Living costs, rent and travel are not mentioned anywhere in the published description
Do not expect a printed figure. HSG defines the value by reference to the current Bachelor tuition fees rather than publishing a fixed amount, so the actual cash value moves with HSG's fee levels

Do not confuse this with the HSG Best Talents Programme. That is a Master's-level scheme restricted to EU/EFTA nationals and Swiss C permit holders. The Bachelor Excellence Scholarships carry no published citizenship restriction, but you must already be enrolled at HSG

Do not confuse this with the HSG Loan and Scholarship Fund or with cantonal scholarships. Those are means-tested routes with different rules, and HSG notes Swiss citizens have a legal right to cantonal scholarships

If you need support before the invitation exists, the Advice Center for Study Funding does provide subsidiary funding, loans and emergency loans, with applications generally possible from the second semester. That is a different track with its own deadlines
Submit well before the deadline. HSG states that forms which have not been duly completed will not be processed, and that the completeness check comes first, followed by a personal interview

If you need partial or total tuition-fee remission in an urgent financial situation, that is a separate route with the same 1 October and 1 March deadlines and a means test based on your and your parents' financial and familial situation
common_rejection_risks: Applying without an invitation from the University of St.Gallen, which HSG states is not possible
Not being enrolled in a Bachelor's degree at HSG when the application is made
Not having outstanding academic performance in the HSG Assessment Year, so no identification and no invitation
Failing funding-source-specific criteria where the funding source applies additional ones
Submitting an incomplete form, which HSG states will not be processed
Missing the Compass deadline of 1 October or 1 March
Not responding to the personal interview the Advice Center coordinates after the completeness check
Expecting living costs to be covered, which the published description does not offer

Travel and relocation costs - not mentioned in the published description
Books, materials, equipment and course-specific extras - not mentioned in the published description

Any residual Bachelor tuition fees if the 6-semester value does not match your full programme length, for example where fees change mid-programme; the award is fixed by reference to the tuition fees current at award
Health insurance, which Swiss residents must arrange themselves and which is not part of the award
Anything beyond 6 semesters, for example a switch to a different programme or a repeat year

official.description: Webster Vienna Private University offers the WVPU New Student Scholarship, a partial tuition award in three tiered levels for newly admitted bachelor's and master's degree students, on the basis of both academic achievement and financial need. Up to 20 awards are made per year at EUR 12,000/7,000/4,000 per academic year for bachelor's degrees and EUR 8,000/5,000/3,000 for master's degrees. The university states explicitly that these are partial scholarships and that the recipient must pay the remaining tuition fee. Application windows are 1 March to 31 May at 13:00 CET for the Fall semester and 1 October to 30 November at 13:00 CET for the Spring semester.
official.coverage: The WVPU New Student Scholarship covers part of tuition fees only - the university states partial scholarships only, with the remaining tuition payable by the recipient - and does not cover living costs, accommodation, insurance or travel; at the Distinction level a bachelor's recipient receives EUR 12,000 per academic year against full programme tuition.

Convert all financial evidence to euros and state which exchange rate you used - Webster Vienna requires this explicitly
Do not submit bank statements; they are not accepted

Submitting bank account statements instead of salary slips or employer/pension confirmations

Essay outside the 1,000-1,200 word range or not answering one of the two published topics
Missing the 13:00 CET cut-off - the deadline time is stated, not just the date
Assuming the scholarship covers living costs, which the university says you must cover yourself

official.description: The Lund University Global Scholarship is a selective, merit-based programme in which Lund University awards approximately SEK 26 million (EUR 2.3 million / USD 2.7 million) in grants each year to high-achieving students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are applying for degree programmes at Lund. Grants may cover part or all of the tuition fees, with the percentage set by the programme and faculty budget rather than the applicant's academic standing, and the page is explicit that scholarships cover tuition fees only and that living costs are not included. Applicants must first apply through universityadmissions.se with the programme as first choice, then submit a Scholarship Motivation Letter of a maximum 600 words through a separate scholarship portal, and the 2026 round closed on 16 February 2026.

official.description: IPOET (International Programme Office for Education and Training) offers 75% tuition fee waivers funded by the Government of Sweden and administered by Chalmers, and Chalmers awarded approximately 33 IPOET scholarships in 2026. The scholarship is a partial tuition-fee reduction of 75% across the four semesters of a two-year programme, rising to 85% in the second and final year for students who excel in their first year, and no funds are transferred to the scholarship laureates.
purpose: Reduce the tuition burden on prospective fee-paying students from non-EU/EEA countries who hold outstanding academic records
Support first-year Master's students at Chalmers University of Technology, funded by the Government of Sweden and administered by Chalmers
study_type: First year of a two-year (four-semester) Master's programme at Chalmers University of Technology
official.degree_award: Full Master's degree. The scholarship is a tuition-fee reduction attached to a place on a Chalmers Master's programme; it is not a degree or a short-term award.
official.duration: Scholarship offers are valid for two years of study (4 semesters, a 2-year programme) under certain conditions set out in the Scholarship Regulations for fee paying students. The tuition reduction may increase to 85% during the second and final year for students who excel during their first year of studies.
official.application_cycle: Annual. The scholarship application period for Master's programmes opens in late November and closes in mid-January, in parallel with the national master's admission round. The key dates page read gives the cycle as late November 2026 to mid-January 2027 for admission in autumn 2027.
official.deadline_central_display: The application period for scholarships administered by Chalmers is open from late November 2026 until mid-January 2027. Chalmers states the scholarship deadline aligns with the programme application deadline, not the deadline for submitting supporting documentation. All deadlines are at midnight CET on the date indicated.
official.deadline_institutional: 1 February 2027 for both paying the application fee or proving fee-exempt status, and for submitting supporting documentation. Scholarship award notifications are sent by e-mail between mid-March and late April 2027, and the first semester's tuition fees must be received by 1 May 2027.
official.deadline_note: Chalmers publishes the closing date only as 'mid-January' without a specific day on the scholarship page; the key dates page places the master's programme application deadline at 15 January 2027, which is the date used for deadline_central because Chalmers states the scholarship deadline aligns with the programme application deadline.

Students who excel during their first year of studies may receive an increased reduction covering 85% of tuition fees during the second and final year of studies. official.tuition_rule: The IPOET waiver is applied by Chalmers directly as a reduction of the tuition fees charged by the University; no funds are transferred to the scholar. The scholar remains liable for the unpaid share of tuition (25% in years one and, unless increased, two, and 15% in the final year where the increase applies) and for all other costs.
official.host_institution_fee: The scholar pays the remaining share of the Chalmers tuition fee that the 75% reduction does not cover, plus the non-refundable application fee to universityadmissions.se.

official.selection_notes: Selection is based on the applicants' relative academic excellence, which primarily includes a weighted average grade of at least 80% but also the home university's stature including position on global ranking lists and the priority order of the application for Chalmers Master's programmes. The ranking of the applied-for Master's programmes is crucial for the assessment of the scholarship application, and Chalmers advises selecting a Chalmers Master's programme as number one (1) priority to maximise the chance of a scholarship. Fields of study are unrestricted. Being granted alternative or complementary funding from external patrons does not affect the possibility of obtaining a Chalmers scholarship, as an applicant's financial status is not taken into account during the nomination process. Chalmers admissions (scholarship committee) cannot give any preliminary notifications; all applicants for scholarships administered by Chalmers are notified by e-mail when the selection is completed, between mid-March and late April.
