Do not be discouraged by waiting. Chalmers states there is no correlation between how early you submit and the likelihood of receiving a scholarship, although applying early expedites the assessment
Do not chase preliminary news. Chalmers admissions (scholarship committee) cannot give any preliminary notifications, so any agent or contact claiming to know early is not speaking for Chalmers

Ignore anyone asking you to pay to apply. Chalmers states explicitly that applying for Chalmers scholarships is free of charge and that you must not follow other links or pay fees in respect of applying

Do not be confused by other Cholarships. The Swedish Institute (SI) scholarships for Global Professionals are not administered by Chalmers and have their own timeline and process. The Avancez, US Friends of Chalmers, Adlerbert Study, COLFUTURO, FIDERH, FUNED, Alfred Ots, WeMakeScholars, LPDP and SI Pioneering Women in STEM awards are separate schemes

A genuine advantage: being granted alternative or complementary funding from an external patron does not affect your eligibility, because Chalmers states an applicant's financial status is not taken into account during the nomination process

Start your residence permit planning around the tuition payment. Chalmers states you cannot start the residence permit application process until you have paid the tuition fees, and the process can take a long time
common_rejection_risks: Being a citizen of an EU/EEA country, and therefore not required to pay Swedish tuition fees
Already being a current student at Chalmers, since these scholarships are for prospective students only and must be submitted before the start of the first academic year
Not being a 1st year Master's applicant
A weighted average grade below 80%
Missing the mid-January scholarship deadline, or the earlier programme application deadline it aligns with
Not paying the application fee or not proving fee-exempt status by 1 February 2027, which alone disqualifies the application
Not uploading all required documents on the universityadmissions.se account by 1 February 2027
Not fulfilling the eligibility requirements for the Master's programme applied for, which removes the applicant from scholarship consideration regardless of the scholarship application itself
Data in the scholarship form that cannot be verified against the universityadmissions.se documents
Using a different e-mail address from the one registered on universityadmissions.se, so the verification code and notifications do not arrive
Missing the verification code because it went to junk mail
Not ranking the Chalmers programme as number one priority
Failing to confirm acceptance by the deadline in the award notification, which forfeits the offer
estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 25% of Chalmers tuition fees in the first year, and in the second year unless the increase to 85% applies
100% of living costs, accommodation and subsistence in Gothenburg - no funds are transferred to scholarship laureates, so this is entirely unfunded
Travel and relocation costs, not mentioned in the published description
The non-refundable application fee payable to universityadmissions.se
Books, equipment, course materials and project costs
Swedish residence permit application and issuance fees, and the processing time lost because the process cannot start until tuition is paid
Any tuition increase during the two-year award period, which would raise the 25% share you pay, since the waiver is expressed as a percentage of the fees
document_audit: All required supporting documents uploaded on your universityadmissions.se account. Chalmers states the list is specific to Chalmers and applies to all applicants including those with a Swedish personal identity number and/or Swedish citizenship, and the list and instructions are published on Chalmers' 'Apply for master's programmes' page
Proof of application fee payment, or documentation of EU/EEA citizenship, by 1 February 2027
Every datum entered in the scholarship form must be verifiable against the documents you uploaded at universityadmissions.se, so check consistency before submitting
No separate scholarship document pack is published for IPOET; the scholarship form is electronic and free of charge
No file type, file size, translation or certification rule is published for the scholarship application; the Master's programme upload rules govern

Download the admission decision PDF 'Notification of Selection Results' when published, as it is the official document and fee-paying students will see 'Conditionally admitted', which persists even after payment

referee_tracking.instructions: Chalmers publishes no referee, recommendation or reference-letter requirement for the IPOET Scholarships. Selection is made on the published academic and ranking criteria by the Chalmers scholarship committee, and no interview is described on the pages read. Do not spend effort arranging referees for IPOET itself. The only third-party input that matters is the prestige of your home university, which Chalmers assesses from its position on global ranking lists rather than from a referee.

alerts.message: The master's programme application period opens on 16 October 2026. Do the universityadmissions.se application first, since the scholarship application depends on its 8-digit number.
The Chalmers scholarship application period opens. You may apply before completing your programme documentation, but the scholarship is only processed once the programme application is complete.
Prepare the application fee and the supporting documents now. Missing either on 1 February 2027 removes the application from consideration.

Two hard deadlines on the same day: application fee paid or fee-exempt status proven, and all supporting documents uploaded. Chalmers states your scholarship application will not be considered if either is missed.
The scholarship portal closes. The scholarship deadline aligns with the programme application deadline, not the documentation deadline. After this point you cannot change the application.
Check your junk e-mail folder for the verification code, which is sent within a few minutes to the address registered at universityadmissions.se.
All applicants are notified by e-mail, whether awarded or not. Chalmers cannot give preliminary notifications, so no news before then is meaningful.
Confirm acceptance by the deadline specified in the notification, following the instructions in it. Failing to confirm forfeits the offer.
First semester tuition balance due to Chalmers. Only after paying can you start the residence permit application, which takes a long time.
Mandatory enrolment in Ladok. Studies begin.

submission_workflow: Confirm you are a non-EU/EEA citizen liable to pay Swedish tuition fees and a first-time Master's applicant
Check your weighted average grade is at least 80% and consider how your home university ranks globally
Submit your Master's programme application at universityadmissions.se between 16 October 2026 and 15 January 2027
Rank your Chalmers Master's programme as number one of a maximum four choices
Pay the application fee or prove fee-exempt status by 1 February 2027
Upload all required supporting documents on your universityadmissions.se account by 1 February 2027
Read the IPOET requirements and the requirements of every other Cholarship you intend to apply for
Open https://scholarship.portal.chalmers.se/ with the same e-mail address as your universityadmissions.se account
Enter your 8-digit application number and the emailed verification code, checking junk mail
Complete and submit the scholarship application by mid-January 2027, verifying that every entry matches your uploaded documents
Amend the application any time before the deadline if needed
Await the e-mail notification between mid-March and late April 2027
If awarded, accept by the deadline in the notification
Pay the remaining first-semester tuition by 1 May 2027 and start the residence permit application
Enrol by 30 August 2027
post_award_requirements: Confirm acceptance of the scholarship offer by the deadline specified in the notification
Pay the remaining share of the tuition fees, with the first semester due by 1 May 2027
Enrol by 30 August 2027; enrolment is a mandatory step
Remain enrolled and studying at Chalmers for the two years covered by the offer, under the conditions in the Scholarship Regulations for fee paying students
Aim to excel in the first year of studies, since the reduction may then increase from 75% to 85% of tuition fees in the second and final year
Start the residence permit application only after paying tuition fees, and allow for a long processing time
No published return-home, deferral, clinical or repayment obligation exists for this award; none is recorded. No funds were transferred to you in the first place

If tuition fees rise during my two years, does my 75% reduction rise with them or stay fixed?
What are the exact conditions in the Scholarship Regulations for fee paying students that make an offer valid for two years?

What are the required documents for my programme, and does any of them need certified translation or an apostille?

official.description: The LiU International Scholarship is aimed at supporting international master's degree students with significant academic potential who are required to pay tuition fees. LiU states the tuition fees for a student awarded a LiU International Scholarship are normally reduced by 50%, offers a limited number of these scholarships to new students, and reserves the right to determine year by year how many scholarships are offered and what percentage is given. The scholarship may cover the total tuition fee or part of it, and the student must pay any remainder by the payment deadline.
purpose: Support international master's degree students with significant academic potential who are required to pay tuition fees at Linköping University
Recruit outstanding new students to master's programmes at Linköping University by reducing their tuition fees
Provide a tuition-fee reduction rather than a living-cost grant, with the scholarship covering the total tuition fee or part of it
study_type: Master's degree study at Linköping University as a new student, normally at a workload of 30 credits per semester with courses included in the programme
official.degree_award: Full Master's degree. The scholarship is a tuition-fee award attached to a master's programme place, not a degree or a short-term award.
official.duration: The scholarship offer is only valid for the specific year and master's programme stated in the Notification of Selection Results. For a master's programme the scholarship or fee normally covers a workload of 30 credits per semester as long as the courses are included in the programme. LiU International Scholarship holders must pass at least 75% of their courses during the first academic year in order to receive the scholarship for the following academic year.
official.application_cycle: Annual. The application period for LiU Scholarships opens each year on the day students receive the Notification of Selection Results and is only open for a short window. For 2026 the window ran from 26 March to 30 March, closing at 23:59 CET, with recipients published on 10 April.
official.deadline_central_display: In 2026, the application period was open from 26 March and closed at 23:59 CET on 30 March. LiU states the application period for LiU Scholarships opens each year on the day students receive the Notification of Selection Results and is only open for a short window. No dates are published for the next cycle.
official.deadline_institutional: Eligible students must already have applied by the deadline for the first admission round, submitted all required documents by the deadline, chosen a Linköping University master's programme as first priority (ranked number 1 of 4), and have been admitted to their first choice in the First Notification of Selection Results, which is usually at the end of March.
official.deadline_note: The only dates published are for the 2026 cycle: opening 26 March, closing 30 March at 23:59 CET, and recipients published 10 April. LiU publishes the rule that the window opens on the day of the Notification of Selection Results, usually end of March, but no calendar dates for the next cycle are published, so no forward-looking deadline_date can be set from official sources.
official.funding_label: LiU International Scholarship - tuition fees normally reduced by 50%, or the total tuition fee; limited number of scholarships for new students, with the percentage and volume determined year by year
official.funding_period: Tuition-fee reduction for the specific year and master's programme stated in the Notification of Selection Results, normally covering a workload of 30 credits per semester
official.tuition_coverage: The tuition fees for an awarded student are normally reduced by 50%. LiU states the scholarship covers the total tuition fee or part of the tuition fee, and that if it covers part of the fee the student must pay the remainder no later than the payment deadline. LiU reserves the right to determine internally, year by year, what percentage will be offered.
official.tuition_rule: Linköping University applies the reduction to the tuition fees it charges. The offer is valid only for the specific year and master's programme stated in the Notification of Selection Results, and normally covers a workload of 30 credits per semester as long as the courses are included in the programme. For any additional courses beyond 30 credits there will be an additional fee. If the scholarship covers only part of the tuition fee, the student must pay the remainder no later than the payment deadline.
official.host_institution_fee: Any tuition fee not covered by the scholarship must be paid by the student no later than the payment deadline, and an additional fee applies for any courses beyond 30 credits per semester. Citizens from countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland must pay application and tuition fees for higher education in Sweden.

The scholarship or fee normally covers a workload of 30 credits per semester as long as the courses are included in the programme

Assume your money must cover everything except half the tuition. There is no published living-cost allowance, no travel coverage and no stipend. Gothenburg or Linköping rent, food, insurance and travel are on you

Treat the 75% course-pass rule as a hard deadline, not a target. LiU assesses only results registered on 1 July of the regular academic year, and explains that studying 60 credits a year means you need 45 completed credits from your programme by 1 July or you lose the scholarship. Over-examining in a later semester does not help

Do not stack the Swedish Institute scholarship with this one. LiU states that applicants awarded a scholarship by the Swedish Institute will subsequently have their Linköping University scholarship rescinded. If the SI is your better route, take the SI

Do not skip the residence permit. LiU states applicants unable to acquire a permit from the Swedish Migration Board in time for the start of studies or the registration deadline will have the scholarship rescinded
Watch your fee-paying status. If your status changes to that of a non-fee-payer the scholarship is no longer valid, and LiU requires you to inform the University in writing

Be realistic about volume. LiU states it offers a limited number of scholarships and reserves the right to decide year by year how many are offered, what percentage, and the merit process itself where more eligible applicants than places exist
Do not overshoot 30 credits a semester without budgeting. LiU states the scholarship or fee normally covers 30 credits per semester and that additional courses beyond that carry an additional fee
Expect the result on the university page, not by email. LiU publishes the list of recipients on the scholarships page, and for 2026 the published date was 10 April

official.description: The Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship offers a 50% tuition fee reduction and is a prestigious, highly competitive award with limited places for students with a high distinction average. It recognises international students commencing undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degrees who have achieved outstanding academic performance in their previous studies. Applications open on Monday 24 August 2026, and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with scholarship offers made throughout the recruitment cycle until all allocations have been exhausted.

For postgraduate applicants, note the ATAR 99 route does not apply to you. The undergraduate-only ATAR 99 threshold and the GPA threshold are listed separately, and only the GPA or comparable score applies to you

Get your comparable score argument in order. A minimum overall GPA of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale, or a comparable score, must be demonstrated in the qualification used as the basis of admission. Prepare the evidence of that comparison rather than assuming it is self-evident

Protect the award from day one. The continuation condition is a Program Term GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 scale in each compulsory Study Period. A single term below can suspend the scholarship, and the suspension mechanism is not simply a make-up opportunity

Note the recovery rule, which is unusual and worth understanding. If your overall GPA falls below the minimum, the scholarship is not applied to the next invoice; if your GPA returns to the minimum or above, it recommences and is applied to the next invoice. So a dip is not necessarily permanent, but you will pay the intervening invoice
Use the free academic support. The University points to the Student Academic Learning Support team and its free academic support services, which is directly relevant to holding the 5.5 GPA

official.description: The UQ International Excellence Scholarship is funded by The University of Queensland and is a tuition fee reduction of 25% per annum for the duration of the enrolled coursework program. It is for high achieving international students commencing a relevant full-time undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program of at least 16 units at UQ in 2027. There is no separate scholarship application: applicants are assessed automatically when they apply to study a program at UQ.

Recognise academic excellence among international students in the pool of offer holders for programs in their commencement semester

official.description: The ANU University Research Scholarship supports high-achieving higher degree by research students whose research aligns with the University's strategic directions, offered through two annual central scholarship rounds that also include the Research Training Program and other centrally managed scholarships. It provides a stipend of $40,475 per annum (full-time base stipend rate 2027) paid fortnightly, plus travel and removal allowances, a thesis allowance, a dependant child allowance for international students and paid medical, maternity and parental leave. No separate application is needed: eligible candidates are considered through their HDR admission application by selecting 'Australia: ANU - Other Scholarship', with international Round 1 applicants required to apply for admission by 31 August.

official.description: doc.funds.connect is an Austrian Science Fund (FWF) programme, run in cooperation with the Christian Doppler Research Association (CDG), that funds joint doctoral training programmes at Austrian universities and Austrian universities of applied sciences. It pays the personnel costs of 5 to 8 doctoral candidate positions plus training costs of up to â‚¬5,000 per doctoral candidate position per year, for a maximum of 48 months. The applicant is a multi-institutional consortium of researchers, not an individual: individual doctoral candidates never apply to the FWF and are recruited by the funded consortium under its own admission and selection procedures.
purpose: Attractive career opportunities for doctoral students help them gain a foothold in promising research fields â€” doc.funds.connect grants fund joint doctoral training programs at universities and universities of applied sciences.

The program facilitates cooperation between institutions, strengthens the research competence of universities of applied sciences, and offers doctoral students additional opportunities for career development.

The main goal of the program is to fund the establishment and expansion of structured doctoral programs based on international standards, developed and organized jointly by universities and universities of applied sciences. These cooperative training and research structures are intended to help provide doctoral students with an excellent education in the long term.

At the same time, the funding also supports the development of research staff at universities of applied sciences according to the Universities of Applied Sciences Studies Act (FHG) and strengthens the cooperation between universities of applied sciences and universities.
Long term, the program aims to interlink basic and applied research and help establish application-oriented basic research.

The announcement is addressed to international students in the DAAD sense ('graduates', i.e. people who already have at least one first academic degree), and the applicant selects their status and country in the portal to see the programmes for which they are eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Restricted to postgraduate architecture-related fields. The first degree must be in Architecture, Interior Design, Monument Conservation and Building in Existing Contexts/Reconditioning of Old Buildings, Urban Design/Urban Development, Landscape Architecture or Landscape Planning. Selected degree programmes must meet minimum Design/Projects ECTS thresholds (45 CP of 120, 34 CP of 90, or 23 CP of 60). Other DAAD scholarship programmes exist for applicants from the field of History of Architecture or applicants with a scientific project. Study visits abroad within a funded programme are only possible under narrow conditions.
official.application_method: Two-step submission, both required: (1) register on the DAAD portal, complete the online application in full and upload the item 1 documents to the portal's 'Attachments' section; (2) if the application passes the formal check, you receive a link to upload work samples to the DAAD media database by 23 October at the latest and must upload them by 4 November CET at the latest. If you already have an admission from a desired degree programme, complete the form anyway and upload it. Do not upload work samples or portfolios to the DAAD portal itself. The portal closes at 24.00 hrs CET/CEST on the last application day.

For English-language degree programmes you must already provide proof of language skills that meet the requirements of your chosen universities with the scholarship application. German-language architecture programmes generally expect at least B2, usually C1; for those, proof of German at a completed B1 level per the European Framework or TestDaF must be submitted.

Complementary studies not leading to a final qualification: one academic year. Start is usually 1 October of the year after the application, or earlier if a German language course is taken prior to the study programme.

Individual fees, dorm damage, parking tickets, library charges and similar are your responsibility

official.tuition_coverage_note: Verbatim: 'Please note that DAAD does not cover tuition fees.' German state colleges of music (Staatliche Musikhochschulen) charge fees, which the applicant must meet.

eligibility: Be a graduate of the field of music

Have obtained a first degree in music by the time the scholarship begins, or have exhausted all training opportunities for your instrument or subject in your home country if no degree is offered in the country of origin
As a rule, your university degree should not date back more than 6 years at the time of the application deadline
Not have resided in Germany for more than 15 months prior to the application deadline
Be in a status and country listed in the DAAD portal selector; if your status or country is not listed you cannot apply
official.citizenship_residency: The call is open to graduates from the field of music in any country listed in the DAAD portal's country selector. 'Country' is defined as the country in which you are living and from which you are applying; if you come from another country, DAAD advises contacting them to find out whether you are eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Explicit: the programme is for international graduates applying from outside Germany, filtered by country and applicant status through the DAAD portal. No country list is printed in the programme body.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Strict. The programme funds only projects in the artistic field at a state college of music (Staatliche Musikhochschule) in Germany of your choice - either degree studies (2nd cycle Master's or 3rd cycle Konzertexamen/Meisterklasse) or advanced studies without a degree with a confirmed German supervisor. Other DAAD programmes exist for musicology, music education, or musicians with a scientific project. A study period abroad within a funded Master's is fundable only if essential, outside your home country, and not exceeding 25% of the scholarship period (up to 50% for joint and double-degree programmes if specified in the study regulations).
official.application_method: Submit a complete online application in the DAAD portal, stating the entire intended scholarship period. Shortly after submitting, DAAD sends a separate link for uploading work samples to the protected DAAD media database; these must be uploaded promptly, within two weeks of receiving the link. Both steps are required for a valid application.

official.description: DAAD's Study Scholarship for Postgraduate Studies in the Field of Music funds graduates of music to take an advanced postgraduate course at a state college of music in Germany of their choice, either a Master's or a 3rd-cycle Konzertexamen/Meisterklasse, or advanced studies without a degree with a confirmed German supervisor. The award is EUR 992 per month plus a one-off study allowance, insurance contributions and, on application, a travel allowance. It funds only artistic projects - musicology, music education and scientifically-oriented musician projects go to other DAAD programmes - and DAAD explicitly does not cover tuition fees.
official.coverage: Covers a monthly stipend, a one-off study allowance, insurance contributions and, on application, a travel allowance and rent subsidy; explicitly does not cover tuition fees at the German college of music or entrance examination costs.

official.description: The Heinrich Böll Foundation funds students from developing and transition countries who pursue a Master's or PhD in Germany. Master's students receive EUR 992 per month, rising to EUR 1,060 from the second year if they work at least 20 hours per week, and doctoral students receive EUR 1,500 per month. The Foundation also funds health insurance, a EUR 38 monthly fringe benefit, and optionally up to EUR 10,000 per year of tuition fees. Applications run 15 January to 1 March for the spring intake and 15 July to 1 September for the autumn intake, and any other income must be declared.

purpose: As seen in the chart below, there are seven types of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship program. They are Research students, Teacher training students, Undergraduate students, Japanese studies students, college of technology students, Specialized training college students, and Young Leaders Program (YLP) students.

The YLP type targets those who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries: university or college graduates who have practical work experience, young public administrators and similar participants who are expected to play an active role.

official.description: Kyushu University does not operate a single named international scholarship for master's and PhD students. Instead, it publishes an annual scholarship information list in which more than 65 awards from external foundations are available to enrolled international students, each with its own stipend amount, duration, deadline and application route. official.description: Entrusted by the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China, the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences recruits outstanding young graduate students from around the world and provides full scholarships through the 2026 Chinese Government Scholarship call. Successful Master's students are exempted from RMB 30,000/year tuition and successful PhD students from RMB 40,000/year, receive monthly stipends of RMB 3,500 and RMB 5,000 respectively, free UCAS Beijing campus accommodation or a housing subsidy of up to RMB 700-1,000/month, and RMB 800 medical insurance, for 36 months. official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The program is administered jointly by CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC as part of the Canada Research Training Awards Suite, which also includes the CGRS D and the Canada Postdoctoral Research Award. You must apply to an institution that has an allocation for your intended field of research; the three fields of research are health, natural sciences and engineering, and social sciences and humanities, and applications deemed by a host institution to be mislabelled will be re-labelled. Awards are tenable only at eligible Canadian institutions, without exception.
official.application_method: Complete and submit an application to up to three institutions using the Research Portal. The agencies direct applicants to the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's program: Instructions for completing an application web page, which sets out all 11 steps. The NSERC page warns that as the deadline approaches, delays may occur due to high volume of users on the Research Portal, and that it is the applicant's responsibility to follow all 11 steps before the portal closes. Selection and post-award administration are carried out at the institutional level under the guidance of the three agencies. You can submit your application in either of Canada's official languages, English or French, and supporting documents in another language require a certified translation.

selection_criteria: Academic excellence (weight 50%): as demonstrated by past academic results, transcripts, awards and distinctions. Indicators: academic record; scholarships and awards held; duration of previous studies; type of program and courses pursued; relative standing if available

Research potential (weight 30%): as demonstrated by research history, interest in discovery, the proposed research, its potential contribution to the advancement of knowledge in the field and any anticipated outcomes. Indicators: quality and originality of contributions to research and development; relevance of work experience and academic training to the field of proposed research; significance, feasibility and merit of proposed research; sound judgment and ability to think critically; ability to apply skills and knowledge; initiative and autonomy; research experience and achievements relative to expectations of someone with your academic experience

Personal characteristics and interpersonal skills (weight 20%): as demonstrated by past professional and relevant extracurricular interactions and collaborations. Indicators: work experience; leadership experience; project management including organizing conferences and meetings; ability or potential to communicate theoretical, technical or scientific concepts clearly and logically in written and oral formats; involvement in academic life; volunteerism and community outreach
official.selection_weighting: Academic excellence 50%; Research potential 30%; Personal characteristics and interpersonal skills 20%

official.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's (CGRS M) is one of three programs in the Canada Research Training Awards Suite, jointly administered by CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC, and it supports up to 3,298 students annually across all disciplines. The value is $27,000 for 12 months, and the merit review is conducted by the host institution against published weights of academic excellence 50%, research potential 30% and personal characteristics and interpersonal skills 20%. Applicants must be Canadian citizens, permanent residents or Protected Persons as of the deadline, and must have completed 0 to 12 months of full-time study in the program for which funding is requested. Applications go through the Research Portal to up to three institutions by 1 December before 8:00 pm ET, and offers are available in the portal from 1 April with alternate offers possible until 31 January of the following year.
official.program_type: Tri-agency government research training award (institutionally administered merit scholarship)
official.region: Canada (eligible Canadian institutions only, without exception)
official.coverage: A $27,000 stipend for 12 months with optional supplements; the published value contains no tuition-fee component, and the pages do not state that tuition, living costs and required expenses are covered, so it is not recorded as fully funded.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your status is Canadian citizenship, permanent residency or Protected Person as of 1 December - this is a hard gate
Identify up to three Canadian institutions that hold a CGRS M allocation in your field of research; applications to institutions without an allocation in your field will be re-labelled or refused
Contact the faculty of graduate studies at each institution for their internal admission deadline, which is earlier than the agency deadline
Count your completed months of full-time study in the program for which you are requesting funding as of 31 December, and confirm you fall in the 0-12 month or the 4-12 month window
Confirm you have not held a Master's-level CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC scholarship, or an Indigenous Scholars Award and/or Supplement
Confirm you are applying to only one CRTAS program this academic year
Ask your institution how it applies the first-class average requirement, since institutions may at their discretion accept applicants who have not obtained one
Start the Research Portal application early - the agencies warn of portal congestion near the deadline and require all 11 steps to be complete
common_rejection_risks: Missing the institutional admission deadline while hitting the 1 December agency deadline - the agencies require you to respect the internal deadline
Applying to more than three institutions, or to institutions with no allocation in your field of research
Being outside the 0-12 or 4-12 month study window as of 31 December, or miscounting part-time study (part-time is calculated proportionally by percentage of full-time course load)
Holding or currently holding another Master's-level tri-agency scholarship, which is disqualifying
Applying to more than one CRTAS program in the same academic year, where only the first eligible application is retained
Portal congestion causing a late submission on 1 December - the agencies state that late applications will not be accepted and that the burden is the applicant's
Missing the English or French submission option, or omitting certified translations of documents in another language
Forgetting to check the Research Portal for results from 1 April onward, with alternate offers possible until 31 January
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees - the $27,000 is a stipend with no published tuition component
Living costs above the $27,000 over 12 months
Bench fees, equipment, computing and fieldwork costs
Health insurance, where not provided by the province or institution
Conference and travel costs, unless you win the CRTAS Research Travel Supplements, which is the only concurrent award permitted

alerts.message: The agencies encourage an IDP, but state explicitly that IDPs are not a CGRS M selection or evaluation criterion, so time spent on one does not improve your score.

submission_workflow: Confirm your Canadian citizenship, permanent residency or Protected Person status as of 1 December
Research which Canadian institutions hold a CGRS M allocation in your field of research and shortlist up to three
Contact the faculty of graduate studies at each shortlisted institution for the internal admission deadline and the first-class average policy

On acceptance, confirm you hold no other tri-agency award, and comply with the award holder's guide

eligibility: You must not be a Canadian citizen nor a permanent resident of Canada, and must not have applied for permanent residence in Canada
You must not have already received a PBEEE

Candidates from Québec, Wallonia and the Maghreb are not eligible. For Québec-Wallonia candidates, having previously studied at a French-language university-level institution in Belgium is a prerequisite
The scholarship period must begin between May 1, 2026 and January 15, 2027

The scholarship is for full-time study, defined as at least 12 credits per half-year for graduate studies, at a Québec university, a CCTT Network institution, or a Canadian or international non-profit research institution, and your supervisor must be a regular staff member of the host institution
Your previous degree(s) must qualify you for the programme you are applying to, and the chosen study option must be a research master's (VM), doctoral or postdoctoral option
The master's programme must lead to a thesis, dissertation, research report or scientific article. An essay, a literature review or a professional master's programme is not eligible
You must comply with the scholarship holder's guide and the rules for use of the scholarship
official.citizenship_residency: 'You must not be a Canadian citizen nor a permanent resident of Canada. You must also not have applied for permanent residence in Canada.' Certain bilateral component agreements restrict eligibility by country of citizenship: 'Component specific bilateral agreements with Brazil, China, India, Israel and Wallonia restrict eligibility by country of citizenship'.
official.international_eligibility: Explicit - open to foreign students who are neither Canadian citizens nor permanent residents and who have not applied for Canadian permanent residence, subject to country-of-citizenship restrictions in specific bilateral components.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Component-specific. The programme comprises 14 sub-components: VM; V1, 1B, 1C, 1I, 1IS, 1W; V2, 2B, 2C, 2I; V3, 3B, 3C, 3I, 3IS, 3W. Some components are for specific degree levels: 1, 2 and 3, along with B, C, I, IS and W, apply to different levels, and the 1B, 2B, 3B components exclude doctorates unless the component expressly states otherwise. Bilateral agreements with Brazil, China, India, Israel and Wallonia restrict eligibility by country of citizenship.
official.application_method: Three stages. (1) The responsible entity, either a Québec university or the CCTT network, submits the nomination form to the FRQ by 23 October 2025 at 4 p.m.; for China Scholarship Council candidates the deadline is 31 March 2026. (2) You create your FRQnet account. (3) The FRQ then contacts you to complete an electronic form and attach the required documents, submitted electronically by 2 December 2025 at 4 p.m. Note that the Toolbox link about the preselection submission date shows as unavailable on the page.

The programme's official working language for applications is French, and no English score or level is published, so none is asserted here.
selection_criteria: The excellence of the applications presented will be assessed by multidisciplinary evaluation committees composed of professors and university researchers

Applications are evaluated according to the evaluation criteria and weighting published in the program rules, illustrated in the page image at https://frq.gouv.qc.ca/app/uploads/2025/08/capture-decran-2025-08-14-180258.png
official.duration: Component-dependent. VM: maximum 6 instalments, 2 years. Doctoral: up to 12 sessions, 3 years, with a reduced rate in sessions 10-12 if extended. Postdoctoral: not renewable, 3 instalments. Short-term: not renewable, maximum 4 instalments.
award_holder_conditions: Must comply with the scholarship holder's guide to the applicable rules
The start of the scholarship period must fall between 1 May 2026 and 15 January 2027; the scholarship is not retroactive and semesters prior to summer 2026 cannot be funded
Scholarship payments only begin once the FRQ receives a copy of the study permit for doctoral candidates, or the work permit for postdoctoral candidates
Must be dedicated full time to the research and to the research activities of the program

Must be physically present in Québec for the entire duration of the scholarship and attend the host university, except for the short-term component and research stays outside Québec authorised by the FRQ

Open access is required: the thesis and peer-reviewed publications produced with scholarship support must be accessible without embargo
Must grant the MES and the FRQ a non-exclusive, irrevocable and non-transferable licence on the final report and research findings
Must acknowledge the financial support of the MES in partnership with the FRQ in publications, notices and interviews
supplements_or_initiatives: Component-specific supplementary scholarships for certain countries and institutions

official.description: The PBEEE (Programme de bourses d'excellence pour les étudiants étrangers) is a merit scholarship from the Québec Ministry of Higher Education and the Fonds de recherche du Québec for foreign students doing full-time research study in Québec, awarded in 14 sub-components. Amounts and duration vary by component, from a $3,000 per month short-term award to a doctoral award totalling up to $87,000 over three years, and the MES adds an exemption from higher foreign-student tuition fees plus RAMQ medical insurance. The 2026-2027 round is marked out of competition and candidates must be preselected by a Québec university, the CCTT network or the China Scholarship Council.
official.program_type: Government research scholarship for foreign students (Québec)
official.coverage: Covers a component-dependent stipend for up to three years, a French-language university tuition-fee exemption for foreign students, and RAMQ medical insurance; it does not cover travel, family or relocation costs, and the physical-presence requirement means applicants must live in Québec throughout.

official.description: The Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) program is a short-term exchange offered by Global Affairs Canada, enabling students from ASEAN member states to conduct study or research at a Canadian post-secondary institution in areas that contribute to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It provides 10,200 CAD for four months or one academic term, funding eligible expenses including airfare, health insurance, living expenses, ground transportation and books. Canadian institutions apply on behalf of candidates through My EduCanada, and the 2025 application period is closed.

official.description: The University of Bologna's study grants and subsidies framework is a portfolio rather than a single scholarship. It combines fee exemptions and reductions (merit-based total exemption for first-year second cycle students who graduated on time with top marks, ERGO means-tested reductions, disability, parenthood and family enrolments), ER.GO regional study grants, '150 hour' collaboration grants, mobility scholarships, and specific international schemes including a reduced fixed fee for citizens of poor, developing and non-EU/non-OECD countries, Unibo for Refugees and MUR-CRUI refugee scholarships. In the Nomination channel, overseas nominating authorities recommend candidates. Host researchers submit through JSPS's electronic application system. Each host researcher may submit up to three applications.

The host researcher may submit up to three applications, prioritising among simultaneous candidates
documents: Electronic application submitted through the JSPS electronic application system
Doctoral degree certificate or diploma, to be submitted before the fellowship starting date
Documents specified in the Application Guidelines for the Standard Program open call
official.english_requirement_note: The JSPS Standard Program pages publish no English language requirement for the candidate or the host institution. Research is conducted at the host institution and the application is submitted in Japanese through the electronic system.
selection_criteria: Open Call: a selection process run by JSPS designates the Fellows from applications submitted by heads of Japanese universities or research institutions wishing to invite foreign researchers
Nomination: overseas nominating authorities recommend candidates
Each round awards approximately 120 fellowships

official.description: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan (Standard) invite young overseas researchers to conduct collaborative research at universities and research institutions in Japan for 12 to 24 months in any field of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences. Each round awards about 120 fellowships, providing a JPY 362,000 monthly maintenance allowance, a round-trip air ticket, a JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance. Applicants are selected either by a Japanese host institution through the Open Call or through an overseas nominating authority.
official.coverage: Covers a JPY 362,000 monthly allowance, round-trip airfare, a JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance; no tuition is listed because the fellow is hosted at a research institution rather than enrolled in a degree programme.

official.description: The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship at NIAS lets researchers and policymakers work on applied monetary economics, macroeconomics and public finance for five to ten months. It is open to prominent mid- to late-career researchers and to promising early-career talents from the Netherlands or abroad, with a minimum of three years of post-PhD experience required, and the Foundation gives particular priority to researchers with an outstanding record in those fields. official.description: Erasmus+ is the European Union programme supporting projects, partnerships, events and mobility in education, training, youth and sport. For individual students its main actions are studying abroad, traineeships abroad and the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees. There is no central application form or central deadline: applications run through the sending university, which selects students fairly and transparently and applies for the funding. Students are exempt from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory/library fees at the receiving institution and receive a grant contributing to travel and daily living costs, with the amount set by national grant agreements.
official.program_type: EU programme grant / mobility scholarship (inter-institutional, no central application)

official.coverage: Erasmus+ covers exemption from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory/library access fees at the receiving institution plus a grant contributing to travel and daily living costs, but the grant is a contribution whose amount depends on living-cost differences, applicant numbers and distance, and small insurance or student-union fees may still apply - so it is not a full cost-of-living package.

official.description: The Fulbright Program in Poland, initiated in 1959 and administered by the Polish-U.S. Fulbright Commission, is a merit-based exchange programme jointly funded by the governments of Poland and the United States. It runs distinct awards in both directions: grants to Poland for US citizens (Scholar, Student, English Teaching Assistant, Specialist, Schuman) and grants to the USA for Polish citizens (Graduate Student up to USD 47,000 for a first year, Junior Research, Polish Scholar, Polish Studies, STEM Impact). Benefits include a stipend, J-1 visa and SEVIS support, medical insurance, a travel allowance and additional allowances for host institution fees, relocation, research and family support, with application windows published as month ranges per award.
official.program_type: Government-funded bilateral academic and cultural exchange programme (US Department of State and Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education)
official.coverage: Covers a living stipend, J-1 visa and SEVIS fees, medical insurance, round-trip travel and additional allowances for host institution fees, relocation, research, conferences and family support, with amounts and duration varying by award; tuition is not stated to be fully covered across all awards.

official.description: CEEPUS, the Central European Exchange Programme for University Studies, is a multilateral exchange programme with Central and Eastern Europe that unites universities from 16 countries within networks of at least three institutions from at least two different contractual countries. Within a network, incoming students are exempted from tuition fees and receive a comprehensive grant from the host country set according to local living costs, with exchanges lasting 3 to 10 months. For the 2027/28 round the central deadline for network applications is 30 November 2026 at 23:59 CET, with an extended deadline of 15 December 2026 for signed letters, and individual mobility decisions rest with the host National CEEPUS Office.

official.description: The PSC Scholarship is the Singapore Government's premier merit scholarship, awarding varied career pathways in the Public Service across Public Administration, Professional Service and Uniformed Service tracks. It covers the cost of degree (tuition fees and other approved charges, plus return airfare for overseas degrees), maintenance and other allowances, and sponsors PSC development programmes including the Preparatory Course, the Mid-Course Programme with an internship, a possible Gap Year and the Public Service Leadership Programme. Holders serve a bond of 4 to 6 years depending on the country of study, and applications for the 2027 cycle are open and close on 15 March 2027.

official.coverage: Covers tuition fees and other approved charges, return airfare for overseas degrees, maintenance and other allowances (full salary for Uniformed Service holders), development programmes, approved exchanges and a sponsored master's if requirements are met, in exchange for a 4 to 6 year public service bond.

official.description: The Lee Kuan Yew Scholarship, set up in 1991 by the Tanjong Pagar Citizens' Consultative Committee with public funding, is Singapore's premier postgraduate scholarship and is open to Singapore citizens. Recipients receive full tuition fees coverage and an annual allowance of S$50,000 for up to 2 years for a Master's degree or up to 5 years for PhD studies, with no restrictions on the course of study and no bond, though recipients are expected to contribute to Singapore society. Applications are submitted through the PSC Gateway portal with a published deadline of 28 February, and the page states applications for the 2026 award are closed.

official.description: SNSF Ambizione supports early-career researchers who want to lead an independent project at a Swiss higher education institution. Grants cover the grantee's salary plus the project funds needed, and run for a maximum of four years, with project starts between 1 September 2027 and 1 September 2028. Applicants may be from Switzerland or abroad provided they meet a four-year (nine-year for medical graduates) post-qualification window and a link with Switzerland. The Call 2026 opened 3 August 2026 and closes 3 November 2026 at 17:00 CET.

official.description: The SNSF Starting Grants are the SNSF's highest level of career funding, enabling researchers to carry out their own independent project and lead a research team in Switzerland. Applicants can request a budget of up to 1 million francs for project funding over five years and can additionally apply for funds to cover their own salary. Eligibility requires a doctorate (or equivalent or medical degree), falling within the eligibility window, not yet having achieved the objective of the call, and a Swiss link of at least two years of research at an average of at least 80% worktime. Evaluation is a two-phase, competition-based procedure with external peer review and interviews.
official.program_type: Career-stage research grant (highest level of SNSF career funding), including the applicant's own salary
official.coverage: Funds an independent research project and team leadership in Switzerland: up to CHF 1 million project funding over five years plus, on request, the applicant's own salary. It is a research grant rather than a student funding package, so tuition and personal living costs are not items it covers.

official.description: The Ministry of Education Short Term Research Awards (STRA) are offered to international scholars, excluding scholars from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao, to encourage them to undertake short term research in Taiwan of 2 to 6 months. Each award provides a monthly research allowance of NTD 25,000 for a Ph.D. student or NTD 40,000 for a postdoctoral fellow, together with economy class round-trip airfare for the most direct route between the awardee's place of residence and Taiwan. Applications for research in the following year must be submitted to the chosen host institution in Taiwan and must arrive there no later than 30 September each year.
official.program_type: Government research visit grant for international PhD students and postdoctoral fellows
official.coverage: Covers a monthly research allowance of NTD 25,000 (PhD students) or NTD 40,000 (postdoctoral fellows) and economy class round-trip airfare for a 2 to 6 month research visit, but the published financial assistance section does not mention tuition coverage, accommodation beyond the allowance, or research costs.

official.description: The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program, a Fulbright exchange funded by the US Department of State and administered by IIE, provides 10 months of professional enrichment and non-degree graduate-level study in the United States for accomplished mid-level professionals from designated countries. Applicants are nominated by US Embassies or Fulbright Commissions, placed in professional-field groups at selected US universities, and complete a six-week professional affiliation, a required seminar and a Global Leadership Forum. Application deadlines vary by country and are set by the embassy or commission.
official.coverage: The pages read do not publish a funding amount or a coverage breakdown, so tuition, living cost and travel coverage are recorded as unstated and fully_funded is false.

Critical Need Language Award of up to $3,000 (optional, separate assessment category)
STEM Supplemental Award of up to $1,000 (optional, separate assessment category)

eligibility: A citizen or national of the United States
An undergraduate student in good standing at an accredited institution of higher education in the United States (two-year or four-year)
Receiving a Federal Pell Grant at the time of application, or able to provide proof that they will receive a Pell Grant during the term of study abroad
In the process of applying to, or accepted to, a credit-bearing study abroad or internship program; proof of program acceptance is required prior to award disbursement
Applying for credit-bearing study abroad in a country or location with an overall US Department of State Travel Advisory Level 1 or 2; specific sub-areas designated Level 3 or 4 are excluded
Not attending a program at an overseas institution on the Section 1286 NDAA List of Foreign Institutions Engaging in Problematic Activities (the list dated 26 June 2026 applies to programs in China)
Recipients can only receive the Gilman scholarship once; a student who previously declined may re-apply if still eligible

official.application_method: Submit the online application through the Gilman application portal by the student deadline. The application requires 4 required short essays (plus optional supplemental essays), transcripts (unofficial and official both accepted), abroad program details (credit-bearing programs only), and selection of a Study Abroad certifying advisor and a Financial Aid certifying advisor. Both advisors must then certify the application in the portal by the advisor certification deadline; applications without both certifications are not considered. Only portal submissions are accepted - no changes can be made after the deadline.

official.description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship is a program of the US Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, funded by the US Government and implemented by the Institute of International Education, that supports Pell Grant-receiving US undergraduates for credit-bearing study abroad or internships abroad. Awards are up to $5,000, with the option of an additional Critical Need Language Award of up to $3,000 and/or STEM Supplemental Award of up to $1,000, and the final amount is set by financial need, program length, overall program cost and the strength of the application. Applications are certified by the applicant's Study Abroad and Financial Aid advisors at the home institution before the program screens eligibility and selection panels recommend candidates for US Department of State approval.
official.program_type: Government-funded undergraduate study abroad grant (needs-based, Pell Grant linked)
official.region: United States (program funds US citizens studying abroad; destination may be worldwide subject to Travel Advisory Level 1 or 2)
official.coverage: Covers part of the student's self-funded study abroad or internship expenses through a needs-based grant of up to $5,000 (plus optional supplemental awards), but does not cover home-institution tuition and does not state that living costs and all required expenses are met.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are receiving a Federal Pell Grant this year, or can document that you will receive one during your abroad term
Confirm your destination has an overall Travel Advisory Level 1 or 2 and that no part of your program sits in a Level 3 or 4 sub-area
Confirm your host institution is not on the Section 1286 NDAA problematic-activities list (the 26 June 2026 list applies to China)
Secure written acceptance into a credit-bearing study abroad or internship program before the deadline
Register your Study Abroad advisor and Financial Aid advisor in the portal, or ask them to register before the deadline
Book a campus visit to the Gilman advisor directory and confirm your advisor is listed for your institution
common_rejection_risks: Missing either of the two advisor certifications by 8 October 2026 - uncertified applications are not considered at all
No Pell Grant and no proof of future Pell Grant eligibility
Non-credit-bearing program, which makes the abroad component ineligible
Destination at Travel Advisory Level 3 or 4, or a Level 3/4 sub-area inside an otherwise Level 1/2 country
Submitting after the deadline; no changes are possible after it closes
Previously holding a Gilman scholarship - recipients can only receive it once
Generic essays that do not name the specific program, destination and follow-on service project
estimated_uncovered_costs: Home-institution tuition and fees for the term abroad
Remaining study abroad program cost above the award ceiling (up to $5,000, or up to $9,000 with both supplemental awards)
Airfare, housing and daily expenses beyond the needs-based award amount
Required travel insurance not reimbursed by the program
Any costs arising if the destination's advisory level changes after award
document_audit: Pell Grant award letter or FAFSA/SFA verification
Unofficial and official transcripts uploaded (both accepted, but unofficial is enough at submission)
Acceptance letter or program acceptance proof for a credit-bearing program
Completed answers to all 4 required essays, with word counts respected
Correct institution, Study Abroad advisor and Financial Aid advisor selected in the portal

official.status_note: The page is live and actively maintained - individual entries carry update dates up to September 2026 (for example 16.09.2026 for the Canon Foundation entry).
official.tuition_coverage_note: The page awards nothing itself and states no coverage. It is a signposting page linking to external funding bodies; the amounts, coverage and rules belong to each linked body.
official.funding_label: Other funding opportunities (information directory, not an award)
official.citizenship_residency: The directory is aimed at students and researchers from Switzerland considering study or research abroad. Individual entries carry their own nationality conditions - for example the Berrow Foundation scholarships are for Swiss nationals domiciled in Switzerland, the Swiss Confederation awards up to four College of Europe scholarships in Bruges and up to SERI-funded places at the European University Institute in Florence, and the SYS Finland study contributions require Swiss nationality or a permanent residence permit in Switzerland.
official.international_eligibility: Varies by entry and is not decided on this page. Several entries are open to applicants from anywhere in a given field - the Canon Foundation in Europe grants up to 15 fellowships a year to highly qualified European and Japanese researchers in all fields.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Not stated. Entry-level restrictions vary: the Canon Foundation covers all fields of research; the Fondation FYSSEN is limited to social anthropology, paleontology, archaeology, ethology, psychology and neurobiology; the Chiang Ching-kuo Foundation is limited to humanities and social sciences; the Centre for Chinese Studies covers humanities and social sciences professors, associate professors, assistant professors and PhD candidates.
official.application_method: Not applicable. The page directs advanced students and researchers to contact the host university directly about financial aid, and states that foreign higher education institutions often offer their own scholarships that are not announced worldwide. Each linked body sets its own procedure.
official.english_requirement_note: No English requirement is published. Entry-level language rules, where any, belong to the linked funding bodies and universities.
supplements_or_initiatives: Information services listed: IEFA.org (updated 26.11.2025), Studyportals (22.10.2025), GlobalScholarships.com (22.10.2025)

Country entries include Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, China/Hong Kong, Estonia, Europe, Finland, France, Germany, Great Britain, Italy, Iraq, Japan, Korea, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Poland, Singapore, Slovenia, Southeast Asia, Sweden, Taiwan, Turkey and the USA

official.description: This is a swissuniversities signposting page, not a scholarship. It collects information about scholarships, grants and funding databases abroad, organised by country or region, and states that swissuniversities occasionally receives such information from higher education institutions, research institutions or foundations abroad. Each entry carries a last-updated date, and the audience is Swiss students and researchers looking to study, research or teach outside Switzerland.
official.program_type: Information directory (no award is made by this body)
official.region: Switzerland (Swiss applicants going abroad); entries cover destinations worldwide
official.coverage: Publishes pointers to third-party funding bodies and scholarship databases; it does not award, administer or guarantee any funding itself.

application_readiness_checklist: Use the page to identify which funding body is relevant to your destination country and field
Go directly to the linked awarding body for the real rules, amount and deadline - this page publishes none of them
Contact your host university directly about financial aid, as the page recommends
Check the 'Update' date on each entry, since links and programmes change

common_rejection_risks: Treating this page as a scholarship with an application and a deadline - it has neither
Assuming any funding is guaranteed because it is listed here
Missing that nationality conditions on most entries restrict applicants to Swiss citizens or residents
Applying to a linked body without reading that body's own current rules
estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything - this page awards nothing
Tuition, living costs, travel and insurance depend entirely on the body you then apply to
document_audit: Confirm the awarding body still runs the scheme before investing effort
Confirm your nationality eligibility for that specific scheme
Confirm the current application deadline on the awarding body's own site

benefits: Grant funding for joint projects and staff/pupil/student mobility between the Czech Republic and Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein
eligibility: Institutional cooperation projects: Czech kindergartens, primary and secondary schools listed in the register of the MEYS; Czech higher education institutions possessing the ECHE (Erasmus Charter for Higher Education)

Mobility projects: Czech kindergartens, primary and secondary schools in the MEYS register; Czech higher education institutions with an ECHE; Czech public institutions operating in school education at national level (National Teaching Institute of the CR, Czech School Inspectorate); regions, municipalities and voluntary associations of municipalities whose scope covers education tasks, including school founders
Vocational education projects: Czech secondary vocational schools and tertiary vocational colleges listed in the register of the MEYS

Inclusive education projects: Czech kindergartens, primary and secondary schools in the MEYS register; Czech higher education institutions with an ECHE; Czech NGOs working in the field of education; Czech public institutions operating in the field of education
In all cases the applicant must be a legal entity: a legal representative of the applicant institution, or a person duly authorised by the legal representative, must sign the application
official.citizenship_residency: Eligibility is institutional and Czech-anchored: applicants must be Czech-registered schools, higher education institutions with an ECHE, or specified Czech public bodies and NGOs. Individuals cannot apply.
official.international_eligibility: Not an individual scholarship. The counterparty side is open to institutions and organisations from the donor states (Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein), with third-country EEA Grants beneficiaries allowed to participate without entitlement to financial support, and Swiss institutions eligible in specific mobility cases.
degree_levels: Not applicable - institutional cooperation grant for schools and higher education institutions, not an individual scholarship
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Restricted to the education sector. The current period focuses on 'supporting and developing civic and pedagogical competences and on strengthening the quality of initial teacher education as well as teachers' continuing professional development.' Project types are limited to Institutional cooperation, Mobility, Vocational education and Inclusive education.
official.application_method: A multi-step online process: read the Call for Proposals and the Guide for Applicants for eligible applicants, partners, activities and eligible expenditure; the Czech institution registers the project application in the online system at eea-app.dzs.cz, with partners given access if needed; the applicant fills in the application and uploads all required annexes using the published Letter of Intent, Work Programme and External Consultant templates; then 'A legal representative of the applicant institution or a person duly authorised by the legal representative must sign the application using the qualified certificate for electronic signature. The application can be signed and submitted only electronically through the on-line system.' First-time registrants need a qualified certificate for electronic signature.

official.description: EEA Grants - Projects and grants is the official DZS page for the Education Programme under the EEA and Norway Grants, which fund cooperation between Czech institutions and those in Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein across four project types: institutional cooperation, mobility, vocational education and inclusive education. Applicants are Czech schools, higher education institutions holding an ECHE and specified public bodies, not individuals, and applications are submitted electronically through the DZS system with a qualified electronic signature. All calls are closed and the last published deadline was 16 February 2022 at 15:00 CET.
official.program_type: Regional cooperation grant programme (EEA and Norway Grants) - institutional, not an individual scholarship
official.region: Czechia, with donor states Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein
official.coverage: Provides grant funding for approved joint projects and for staff, pupil and student mobility between the Czech Republic and the donor states; it is not payable to individuals and does not function as a tuition or living-cost scholarship. Project budgets and eligible expenditure are governed by the individual Call for Proposals and Guide for Applicants rather than by this page.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are applying as an eligible Czech institution, not as an individual - individuals cannot be applicants

Obtain a qualified certificate for electronic signature (for example from Prvni certifikacni or Ceska posta) well before submission
Build the application from the published Letter of Intent, Work Programme and External Consultant templates
common_rejection_risks: Applying outside a call window, since all calls are closed and none is currently announced
Failing the mandatory electronic signature requirement - the application can only be signed and submitted electronically
Uploading a modified template instead of the published one, which the call specifies
Proposing an ineligible partner country or a partner that is an arm of the applicant
Missing the priority themes (democracy, active citizenship, inclusive education) in the project design
estimated_uncovered_costs: Co-financing required of the applicant institution, which is set by the individual call and Guide for Applicants and is not published on this page
Any individual participant costs, since this is an institutional grant rather than a personal award
document_audit: Check every annex required by the call is uploaded, since the online system is the sole submission route
Verify your institution's registration status (MEYS register, or ECHE for higher education) is current at the deadline
Reconcile the draft Partnership Agreement against the published template and Guidance before uploading

official.deadline_note: This is a hub page covering three separate programmes with different deadlines. The Fulbright Foreign Student Program and Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program both closed on 3 August 2026 for the 2027-2028 competition, with the next application deadline given as August 2027 for the 2028-2029 academic year. The Medicus Student and Scholar Exchange Program has a different, later cycle: March 2027 for the 2027-2028 academic year. The recorded date is the Fulbright Foreign Student deadline because it is the only precise one published.

official.funding_duration: 4-10 months
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'The grants are to be used toward the cost of tuition and other academic expenses. For two-year master's programs and Ph.D. programs, the Fulbright grant is awarded for the first year of study and is not renewable.' The stated amount is an estimate: 'In general, a grant for one academic year is about $20,000. However the final grant amount awarded per grantee depends on the number of finalists and on the availability of funds.'
official.funding_label: About USD 20,000 for one academic year (Fulbright Foreign Student), plus J-1 visa sponsorship and health/accident insurance up to USD 100,000 per incident
benefits: Grant of about USD 20,000 for one academic year (4-10 months), not renewable
Health and accident insurance under the Accident and Sickness Program for Exchanges, maximum USD 100,000 per incident
J-1 exchange visitor visa, with IIE covering application fees and negotiating partial tuition waivers or additional financial support at the host university

eligibility: Swiss citizenship (holders of another citizenship must contact the Fulbright Commission or the US Embassy Public Affairs Section in their country of citizenship)
Undergraduate degree from a University or University of Applied Sciences and Arts completed by summer 2027
Applying to pursue a Master's or Ph.D. degree, non-degree coursework, or Ph.D. research in the United States
official.citizenship_residency: 'Swiss citizenship (If you hold another citizenship you must contact the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section in your citizenship country)'. Not eligible: currently studying at a Swiss university without Swiss citizenship; dual US citizenship; US residence; US green card.
official.international_eligibility: The programme is administered for Swiss citizens studying abroad; it is an outbound Swiss grant, not for international students coming to Switzerland. Holders of other citizenships are directed to the Fulbright Commission or US Embassy in their own country.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: 'Applications will be accepted in all fields, except medicine (not including Public Health or medical research), dentistry, and veterinary medicine.' Candidates whose study or research involves medical education or training, clinical or direct patient/animal contact, or required practicum components are excluded. 'Candidates with a Bachelor's or Master's degree from universities of applied sciences and arts as well as candidates focusing on science, technology (e.g., AI, quantum, biotech), engineering, and mathematics are particularly encouraged to apply.'
official.application_method: Complete the online application at the IIE portal, following the Switzerland-specific 'Online Application Instructions'. A complete application consists of the online form including three reference letters uploaded directly by the recommenders plus copies of academic transcripts and diplomas/degrees in English or with an original English translation, AND hard copies of official (certified) academic transcripts with original English translations sent directly from the higher education institution to swissuniversities in a sealed envelope. 'Your application is not considered complete until swissuniversities has received your electronically submitted online application and the hard copies of the official (certified) transcripts.'

selection_criteria: Pre-selection is based on the application materials, in which the personal statement plays an important role

Willingness to consider a mix of small, large, public and private universities and to cooperate with the placement process
Special preference for candidates showing good academic performance, a sincere interest in the US culture and values, and no extensive recent experience of living and studying in the US
Strong candidates are often socially engaged in community service and volunteer activities
Interview before the Fulbright Selection Committee at the US Embassy in Bern in early September 2026

official.description: This swissuniversities hub covers two scholarship programmes for study or research in the United States: the US State Department-sponsored Fulbright Program (both the Foreign Student Program for Swiss graduates and Ph.D. students and the Visiting Scholar Program for Swiss researchers) and the Medicus Student and Scholar Exchange Program funded by the Swiss Benevolent Society of New York. The Fulbright Foreign Student Program awards about USD 20,000 for a 4-10 month non-renewable grant, plus J-1 visa sponsorship, insurance up to USD 100,000 per incident, and IIE university placement. The 2027-2028 Fulbright competition closed on 3 August 2026; Medicus applications for 2027-2028 are due in March 2027.
official.program_type: Government-sponsored outbound study and research grants (administered by swissuniversities for Swiss citizens)
official.coverage: For Fulbright, about USD 20,000 for one academic year applied toward tuition and other academic expenses with insurance and J-1 visa support, but explicitly not renewable and not a full tuition guarantee; the Medicus amount is not published on the hub page.

common_rejection_risks: Submitting the online form without the sealed hard-copy transcripts arriving by the deadline - the application is explicitly incomplete until both are received
Fields of medicine, dentistry or veterinary medicine, and any study involving clinical or patient/animal contact

Already holding admission to a US programme for 2026-2027 and intending to defer it - not eligible
Listing only highly selective US universities, which counts against you
Omitting the Fulbright-mission dimension from the personal statement, which is a stated selection criterion
Extensive recent experience of living or studying in the US, which reduces your score
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition beyond what the grant and any negotiated partial tuition waiver cover
Living costs in excess of the grant for a multi-year programme, since the grant covers only the first year and is not renewable
Family travel - DFAT-equivalent funding here covers individual Fellows only and the Fulbright programme does not fund or support family members
Language testing costs, offset only by vouchers awarded after selection
document_audit: Verify every transcript and degree document is in English or accompanied by an original English translation
Confirm the institution's postal/courier delivery will arrive by 3 August 2026, not merely be posted
Check the IIE portal shows all three reference letters as received before the deadline
Have TOEFL/IELTS booked early enough for results to reach IIE by mid-October 2026, even though the test can follow the application deadline

official.description: The University of Copenhagen offers a limited number of tuition waivers and grants through the Danish Government Scholarship programme for highly talented students with outstanding academic records from non-EU/EEA countries. There is no individual scholarship application: all non-EU/EEA applicants to MA/MSc programmes are automatically considered as part of the academic assessment, and awards are made solely on academic achievement, with financial need explicitly not taken into consideration. The scholarship takes the form of full or partial tuition fee waivers and/or an amount covering basic living expenses, with faculty-specific caps: the Faculty of Science funds tuition plus 22 months of living expenses for applicants above a 90% bachelor's GPA admitted to their first-priority programme, Health and Medical Sciences and Humanities run smaller automatic schemes, Social Sciences offers roughly 2-3 per year only on the September intake, and Theology grants partial tuition waivers only.
