official.description: The BI International Baccalaureate Scholarship is awarded to applicants who graduate with the top grades from the International Baccalaureate programme and covers 100% of tuition fees for up to three years, subject to academic progression. BI states that scholarships are awarded on academic excellence and not on financial need, with a minimum of 33 IB points for consideration, and only candidates admitted to the Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Data Science for Business or Bachelor of Digital Business commencing Autumn 2026 are considered. Applicants must apply for the scholarship at the same time as admission, uploading a combined one-page PDF of CV and scholarship letter into the Scholarship section, and decisions are made in two rounds at the end of April and in July.

official.description: Master Mind Scholarships are granted by the Flemish government to excellent students who want to follow a master's programme at a Flemish higher education institution, to promote Flemish higher education as a top study destination for international talent. The total budget for 2026-2027 is EUR 480,000 and an estimated 30 international students can benefit, with a maximum award of EUR 10,225 per academic year for one year (60 ECTS) or two years (120 ECTS). Applicants must have a GPA of 3.5 out of 4.0 and the stated English proficiency, be nominated by a single host institution, and have their file submitted through Mobility-Online by 27 April 2026 at 23h59 GMT+1.
official.coverage: Provides a maximum of EUR 10,225 per academic year as a cash award, with the host institution permitted to charge a tuition fee of EUR 136.50 for 2026-2027, but does not cover tuition fees, accommodation, living costs beyond the award, or travel.

selection_criteria: Relevant experience and achievements obtained within and beyond academia, weighted up to 40% - assessed through transcripts, other academic accomplishments, prior scholarships and awards, publications and presentations, research and/or creative productivity, academic training and relevant work experience including co-op, and academic, professional and extracurricular activities such as teaching, mentoring, supervising or coaching, managing projects, science or research promotion, community outreach, volunteer work or civic engagement, chairing committees or organizing conferences

Plan of Study, weighted up to 30% - motivation, creativity, communication skills, feasibility, merit and significance; a course-based statement of intent or a research-based research proposal; connection or synergy with the programme of study; for research proposals, the focus and feasibility of the research question and objectives, the clarity of the proposed methodology, and the significance and expected contributions to research

Academic assessment reports, weighted up to 30% with 15% for each letter - ability to complete projects within an appropriate time period, contribution to research and development, critical thinking, application of skills and knowledge, judgment, originality, initiative, autonomy, enthusiasm, and ability to communicate clearly and logically in written and oral formats
Prior scholarships and awards may be used to confirm assessment based on other aspects of the file, but students should not be penalized for not having received other awards

At the graduate unit's discretion, exceptions may be made for highly meritorious applicants below the GPA minimum, for example applicants with documented medical issues or family care responsibilities, applicants who pursued alternative career paths, or mature students with professional experience

official.description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship encourages excellence in graduate studies at publicly-assisted universities in Ontario, and the U of T program is jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University of Toronto, which is allocated a fixed number of awards annually. The award is worth $5,000 per session, so $10,000 for two consecutive sessions or $15,000 for three, with the awarding graduate unit contributing one third of the total, and is tenable for one year. Applicants need an A- or equivalent in each of the last two completed years, must be registered full-time in an eligible two- or three-term programme, and are assessed on relevant experience and achievements (up to 40%), plan of study (up to 30%) and two academic assessment reports (up to 30%). Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons qualify, and international students on valid study permits compete for a set number of awards through a centralized adjudication of graduate unit nominations, with results in mid-July.
official.program_type: Government-funded merit-based graduate scholarship (province-university funded) with a centralized university adjudication
official.coverage: A value-based scholarship of $5,000 per session for two or three sessions ($10,000 or $15,000 per year), with the graduate unit contributing one third of the cost; it is not described as a tuition waiver, and any funds left after tuition charges are refunded.

official.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for up to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. The 2027 call opens on 1 January 2027 at 12:00 PM, closes on 15 April 2027 at 12:00 PM, and results are announced on 31 May 2027 at 12:00 PM. official.description: The VU Fellowship Programme is a merit-based tuition fee waiver from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, with the university having committed approximately one million euros to attract highly motivated and excellent students. It is intended for talented prospective non-EU/EEA students who hold a non-EU/EEA passport, are not eligible for the lower tuition fee, are not of Dutch nationality, prove a bachelor's GPA equivalent to a Dutch 8, and are conditionally or unconditionally admitted to the first year of a full-time English-taught Master's programme starting September 2027; February starters and joint programmes not administered by VU are excluded. Applying for the VUFP also applies the candidate for the NL Scholarship, a EUR 5,000 contribution to living costs for the first year. The programme application opens 1 October 2026 with an advised deadline of 1 December 2026, the VUFP application runs 1 November 2026 to 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET, results are expected mid-March 2027, and offers must be accepted by the end of March 2027.
official.program_type: Institutional merit-based tuition fee waiver for international master's students
official.coverage: Covers tuition fees only, for one or two academic years, with second-year extension conditional on 100% of ECTS; VU states expressly that it provides no allowance for living costs such as rent, food or insurance, which the applicant must finance.
